#3371. After 53 Years, Charlie Brown’s OG Thanksgiving Special Actor Finally Gets Crucial Payments

The actor behind one of the Peanuts franchise's most beloved holiday specials finally gets the recognition he deserves decades later.

A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving is still considered a holiday classic over fifty years after its initial debut. The animated special originally premiered on CBS in November 1973, just two days before Thanksgiving. And, it remains one of the most recognizable installments of the franchise's massive collection of holiday specials.

More than fifty years after A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving made its TV debut, one of the original voice actors behind the titular character has revealed a shocking behind-the-scenes detail about the iconic holiday special. Todd Barbee, who voiced Charlie Brown in several Peanuts projects throughout the 1970s, went decades without receiving residual payments for his work on the massive franchise.

During an interview on Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia, Barbee discussed his experiences working on the hit animated property and revealed that he only started receiving residual payments around six years ago. Despite the continued popularity of the specials, the former child actor had not received any compensation beyond what he was paid to play the role in these productions.

However, Barbee made it clear that he and his co-stars were very well paid for their original recording work. He explained that the amount he earned from just the Peanuts specials alone was enough that he was able to help his mother buy a house, which she still lives in to this very day.

Although Barbee's residual payments arrived decades after his time with Charlie Brown and his friends ended, the actor said that he appreciates the additional income. While the payments are not very large, they are still helpful, and he looks forward to receiving them every year.

Barbee's involvement with the Peanuts franchise extended beyond the Thanksgiving special. Between 1972 and 1974, he portrayed Charlie Brown in four other projects, You're Not Elected, Charlie Brown, There's No Time for Love, Charlie Brown, It's the Easter Beagle, Charlie Brown!, and It's a Mystery, Charlie Brown.

Barbee's history with Peanuts began several years before he landed the role. He previously auditioned for It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown, which premiered in 1966. His father also worked for TV producer Lee Mendelson, who was handling the auditions. However, Barbee was ultimately not cast in that specific special.

A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving and all other Peanuts specials can currently be streamed on Apple TV.

#3370. ‘The Hunting Wives’ Review: Season 2 Reloads Without Slowing Down in Netflix’s Delirious Soap

Amid all the sex and murder in “The Hunting Wives” Season 2 — and there is a lot of sex and murder — the riskiest scene suspends itself between the two. Sophie (Brittany Snow), an East Coast liberal out of place in the conservative Texas town of Maple Brook, and Margo (Malin Åkerman), the mysterious local matriarch who can wrap just about anyone around her finely manicured fingertips, are confronted with a fresh dilemma. For spoilers sake, I won’t get into specifics, but the issue is urgent and impacts them both, without being serious enough to warrant what turns out to be their first-thought fix:

In the moment, their lethal instinct seems reasonable. Margo already shot a pregnant teenager in the woods, and Sophie committed vehicular homicide against Margo’s brother (which invited suspicions about Sophie’s past, considering its eerie similarities to a deadly “accident” back in Massachusetts). Their friends, neighbors, and even a youth pastor met their maker, too — just in the first season! So what’s one more body to bury? Go on! Kill ’em! Get yours! Related Stories ‘The Lowdown’ Season 2 Finale Hinges on Two Monologues — Let Ethan Hawke and Sterlin Harjo Break Them Down Will Ferrell Golf Comedy ‘The Hawk’ Canceled at Netflix After Just One Season

But before their bloodlust gets the best of them, their better angels make one last plea. Margo hesitates. Sophie follows suit. The gears start turning as they stare into each other’s wide, worried eyes: Are they really prepared to take another life? Are people that disposable to them? What does their initial response say about how they’ve changed? What does it mean about who they’ve become?

No need to spoil what happens next. The pause makes all the difference. “The Hunting Wives” has always been self-aware, but Margo and Sophie’s recognition of slaughter as their default response to trouble is a critical moment in a second season that reloads without slowing down. Creator Rebecca Cutler knows her Netflix soap is careening past the point where its central couple can reasonably return to lives lived between Margarita Mondays and Sunday church. Killing again, so quickly and carelessly, puts them on the precipice of becoming Bonnie and Clyde Bonnie — known fugitives who are only out for each other. Taking a beat lends the series a critical perspective — a vantage point from the top of the roller coaster, right before the big drop, where you can appreciate for a few brief, fleeting seconds the insanity to come.

Then you’re flying. You (and Margo and Sophie) are convinced it’s better to just move forward. Heck, this crisis isn’t going to fix itself!

Margo and Sophie’s breakneck pace to break necks is mostly a feature in Netflix’s surprise hit. The high-key camp comedy and low-key conservative satire moves quickly, sure, but where its characters are often flustered and panicked, it’s decisive in a way that exudes confidence. Progress is fast but assured. The drama is elevated but mindful. Characters don’t ask for permission or forgiveness; they just go after what they want, what they need, or what they feel they have to have, creating a propulsive viewing experience that zips by in a (muzzle) flash.

It’s a welcome change from prestige dramas that regularly feel like they’re stalling for time. While other shows tout firearms around for so long it’s like they’ve never heard of Chekhov, the hunting wives pull the trigger like they’re expecting money to come out — or lovers. Before you can think, “Wait, are they gay, too?” the person in question is already bending their same-sex partner over a desk. Even Season 2’s in-media-res opening lasts only a few seconds — like it’s flipping the bird to streaming TV’s favorite plot device — giving just the briefest glimpse of cop cars racing up to a giant cabin where Margo is (supposedly) being held hostage and Sophie is (supposedly) with her, holding a gun.

The opening tease only gets funnier as you find out how much unfolds between the start of the season and the flash-forward, especially considering its implication — that Sophie would threaten Margo’s life — makes sense from the start. Sophie begins Season 2 trying to repair her marriage to Graham (Evan Jonigkeit) and distance herself from Margo. The former goal sees her going to counseling sessions (where she comically compares her family to a box she wants to be trapped in), running errands, and playing the dutiful housewife.

The latter goal is harder and, arguably, more important. Margo doesn’t know her brother is dead. He’s not answering her calls or texts, but that’s hardly unprecedented behavior, so Margo ignores it — until the leader of a motorcycle gang (Dale Dickey!) shows up, claiming Kyle owes her, and if he doesn’t pay, she’ll take what she wants from Margo.

There’s never a good time for angry bikers to roar up your driveway demanding money, but it’s a particularly bad time for Margo. She’s in the doghouse with Jed (Dermot Mulroney) over the whole “a high schooler got me pregnant and then I had an abortion” issue, but a) that means she’s living in the pool house, not the poor house, and b) he’s really only mad because it’s a potential threat to his run for governor, which is gaining steam. Margo tries calling and texting Sophie, but she’s not answering. She wants to believe she doesn’t need Margo, love Margo, that she maybe even hates Margo. But a few cleverly laced connections make it clear she can’t.

Outside our core couple, Season 2 introduces plenty of plotlines that could pull them together and/or tear them apart. Callie (Jaime Ray Newman) doesn’t see why welcoming a camera crew to film her friends for a reality show (“Married Justice”) could lead to problems, even when the flirty producer warns participants that they should assume they’re “always on camera.” Her husband and co-star, Sheriff Jonny (Branton Box), is just as foolishly carefree, despite Deputy Wanda (Karen Rodriguez) investigating another dead girl in the woods — aka giving Callie a reason to ask questions about the last dead girl in Maple Brook, aka the aforementioned pregnant high schooler Margo killed.

Speaking of people Margo would prefer to forget, her former boy-toy Brad (George Ferrier), is having a hard time at Baylor. He can’t get over the recent murder of his mother, and his lonely boy coping mechanisms (playing acoustic guitar) soon attract the wrong kind of attention: a predatory music mogul named Chase (John Stamos) who promises to make Brad forget all his worries by turning him into a star (right after he loads him up with booze and drugs).

How Cutler shifts the puzzle pieces around to exert pressure proves just as engaging as before. There are plenty of big, loud laughs to go along with a steady supply of sly jokes and juicy melodrama. Anyone tuning in for the soap should be satisfied, just as anyone eager for some edgy satire should find it.

So long as they’re as open as these characters. “The Hunting Wives” may don MAGA drag to tell its story, but it’s a savage critique of conservative values. There’s Brad’s holier-than-thou father, Reverend Clint (Jason Davis), whose over-reliance on Old Testament discipline masks a hands-off parenting style that feeds his desperate son to the wolves. There’s Jed’s hypocritical right-wing politician, who’s more than OK with a little murder if it helps his campaign (knowing his constituents wouldn’t hold it against him) but can’t abide by his wife’s emotional outbursts in the pursuit of personal independence.

Then there’s the fun fact that everyone is gay (or bi or curious). So much of the show’s tension stems from secret trysts that only need to stay secret because of Maple Brook’s pervasive intolerance. That goes double for Sophie and Margo, whose continued pursuit of their repressed desires manifests in bigger and bigger risks. They get a small taste of what their lives could be like if they could just follow their hearts, sans consequence, forever, and then someone comes along to remind them why they can’t. It so often feels like there’s no real hope for the life they want that they fight like hell for whatever sliver they think they can sustain.

That fight gives the series its heart and its haste, but not everything fares better at a high velocity. By season’s end, Margo and Sophie’s individual interiority is rooted in too many questions and not enough answers, while their relationship feels more symbolic than genuine. Perhaps that’s the point. Perhaps the couple isn’t fated to be together as much as they’re fated to go further alone. Perhaps their relationship is more of a means to an end; a reminder of how far off track they got when they were isolated, and how hard it is to get back on track when the world is working to keep them apart.

Either way, it’s good drama. Either way, they’re going to discover new sides of themselves. Either way, the coaster is already racing ahead. Maybe it jumps the tracks, maybe it doesn’t. Maybe after all that, they really should just keep killing.

“The Hunting Wives” Season 2 premieres Thursday, November 26 on Netflix. All eight episodes will be released at once.

With a massive wave of mysteries and crime thrillers taking over movies, television, and even the world of podcasts, it was only a matter of time before somebody twisted the formula to make a lighter, more fun experience out of it. Mistletoe Murders, for those who aren't familiar, is about a woman named Emily Lane who moves to a small town and opens a year-round Christmas store — just in time for a series of murders to strike the usually quiet town. It's a simple premise, but it has understandably become a holiday season staple for many over the past three years. It began airing on Hallmark Channel back in 2024, and has released a new season each year as the holidays begin. Unlike the original movies on Hallmark that have to fit their stories into right, 82-minute windows each time, Mistletoe Murders has made great use of its format and allowed the mysteries themselves to simmer a lot more. It's the perfect blend of Hallmark's Christmas tone and the TV mysteries that air year-round.

#3368. 33 Years Later, Calvin And Hobbes’ Darkest Quote On Family Is Still Undefeated

Calvin and Hobbes contains multitudes as a fantastic comic strip from the 1980s and 1990s, with Bill Watterson's work still celebrated over 30 years since it concluded. It's loaded with approachable philosophical insights and emotional nuance, while told largely through the eyes of a chaotic, complicated young Calvin accompanied by his stuffed tiger, Hobbes. While Calvin has plenty of his own high and low points, though, the sometimes underappreciated aspects of living around or even raising a complex young kid can show itself in occasional instances.

Susie Derkins has certainly been expressive about the difficulties of growing up with Calvin as a classmate and friend, but as for family, it can sometimes show in more bite-sized moments. Calvin's parents, naturally, face each little detail head-on, from general mischief, to house damages, to occasional reminders that, while they invest their lives in raising him, he may amusingly not always realize the work that goes into parenting. But for one November 8, 1993 Calvin and Hobbes strip, Calvin attempts to present himself and his parents' work as a point of pride to his mother, with the comic hilariously cutting to her subsequent reaction.

The scenario is incredibly simple for this two-panel strip: Calvin steps in while his mother works on some household errands at the table, simply saying he's her "big accomplishment in life!" This is immediately followed by the father arriving home from work to see mom, sunken into the couch, simply remarking, "I'm depressed." It's effective, incredibly concise, and a funny, lighthearted jab at how parents might occasionally feel like everything they sink into raising their kid might not have been enough. Calvin's an expressive, individualistic young kid with a wild imagination and a heart for mayhem with little responsibility, but he's also, crucially, still a kid, which his parents obviously acknowledge.

It's not that Calvin's mom regrets having him, although moments like this are rare blips of regret to which any parent can relate. It's entirely human to have small moments of doubt in oneself as a parent, especially since Calvin's mother is a stay-at-home mom, so any doubts in raising her boy as the "big accomplishment" of her lifetime are perfectly reasonable. But it's pretty clear from how she's written throughout Calvin and Hobbes that the mother is a proud parent, guilty only of being overwhelmed and exasperated by her son's antics. The best part is, the week surrounding this particular strip alone is loaded with fun moments featuring her.

In the very next strip released on November 9, 1993, Calvin and Hobbes introduced one such type of incident that would understandably overwhelm all sorts of veteran parents. The strip shows Calvin talking to his mother as she goes through his laundry, having taken in some sort of scary critter, erroneously keeping it in his pockets, and being concerned that she didn't find it, implying it's loose somewhere in the home.

The mom understandably grows concerned by Calvin's carelessness, but never outright takes it out on him. Yet, when unprovoked in other strips in that same week, this same character can happily poke fun at her son when tensions are low, her comedic timing staying on-point while not at any point hurting her child's feelings with her wit.

Every great comic strip has to start somewhere, and Bill Watterson's Calvin and Hobbes started off with a cartoon that was almost perfect.

This is the sign of an effective parent who, while never fully adjusted to the whimsy of raising Calvin, shows enough poise at the right moments with him, while channeling any doubts away from him. Calvin's mom is still prone to completely understandable reactions to her son's most foolish actions. But kids are allowed to be loud, annoying, and irresponsible, while parents are allowed to feel overwhelmed or doubt themselves, on the assumption that it doesn't consume them or harm their bonds with their children.

Parents should also be honest with themselves, while being strategic with their hilarious or embarrassing but ultimately harmless truths about their kids, such as confirming that Calvin was, indeed, a very stinky baby. Calvin and Hobbes may largely be about life as a kid, but it also encompasses what goes into raising that kid with love, devotion, and some lighthearted, teasing when the moment calls for it.

#3367. Things 3.25 update brings new touch features to the MacBook Pro

Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

Say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The update follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

The first four episodes, half of the entire season, were released two weeks ago, with two more episodes following weekly until the Season 3 finale earlier this week. Not that the show needed a viewership bump, as it had already been in the #1 spot for days on Prime Video, but Amazon announced mere hours before releasing the final two episodes of Season 3 that the show had been renewed for Season 4. Still, many fans are hoping to see Prime Video adapt a more traditional release schedule for The Rings of Power next season, so the show will be around for more than just a few weeks before disappearing for another two years.

#3365. How Disney’s ‘Hexed’ Reinvents the Witch Through Animation

Every visual element in animation helps tell the story. That’s especially useful when you’re trying to do something new inside the long, proud tradition of Disney animated movies where magic is afoot. “Hexed” is exactly that: the story of a young girl named Billie (Hailee Steinfeld) who learns there’s more to life than her small-town Ohio hometown and more to her family, particularly her mother Alice (Rashida Jones), than meets the eye.

And by “more,” we mean witches. Lots of witches.

“Hexed” builds on work that writers Jared Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller have done with Disney movies like “Encanto” and “Moana,” and that directors Fawn Veerasunthorn and Josie Trinidad (along with co-director Jason Hand) have done with “Raya and the Last Dragon” and “Frozen 2,” among others. In a way, much of it feels familiar to recent Disney Animation Studios fare: A secret world of wonder and magic awaits just around the riverbend and/or through a magic portal, accessible only by imbuing one’s inner spark with “witchification.” But there is still something fundamentally broken about that magic world that our protagonist is positioned to make happen. Related Stories How Much of Quentin Tarantino’s Scrapped Film ‘The Movie Critic’ Made It Into ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’? Robert Aramayo’s Star-Making Turn in ‘I Swear’ Is Already Award-Winning, Now He Just Wants People to See It

And by “something,” “Hexed” Celeste (Jodie Foster), the queen of the hidden realm of Hexe, who is waiting to complete a moonlit ritual that will change the world forever.

According to Miller, the “Hexed” team differentiates this world from the magic of others in the Disney Vault through character design. “ If you look at Billie, you look at Alice, and you look at Celeste, I think we see their personalities come forward,” Miller told IndieWire. “With Alice in particular, she wears this impractical, tight, fitted skirt suit. For me, that was always indicative of the way she is trying to control everything around her, including herself. Even the way she does her hair, she is trying to make sure that her world is safe and contained.”

But the world isn’t safe or containable, and that’s part of the character design, too. Billie doesn’t just have a sparkle in her eyes — he has a crescent moon, hinting at the importance she may hold in completing Hexe’s magic.

“The crescent moon was something that was done in Vis Dev, and then the lighting department told us, ‘We can track that all the way through,” Veerasunthorn told IndieWire. “[It hints at] something special and witchy about Billie, even though she doesn’t know that about herself yet. The way that you see her hair curled in the same shape of the crescent moon, too, is speaking to someone who is looking to fulfill her potential.”

Billie’s design, from the reflection of the moon in her eyes to the color and shape of her hair to the natural elements woven into her clothes, hints at her tendency toward witchiness — and toward belonging in a world she doesn’t even know she belongs in. “We as the audience, we can be like, ‘Girl, figure yourself out!’” Veerasunthorn joked.

Both Billie and Alice are designed in stark contrast to Celeste, who perhaps has too much figured out in terms of witch magic and her silvery, flowing, regal appearance. “[Celeste’s] magic is elegant and powerful, very controlled,” Veerasunthorn said. “The color of Alice’s magic is in between these two extremes, and we wanted to get the sense that there’s something broken about her magic that we don’t quite understand yet. There’s a lost-and-found quality, and hopefully subconsciously we’re hoping that she can put her magic back together.”

“What was a challenge was that it’s this world of magic, a world of witches, and we’ve seen that a lot in media,” Trinidad told IndieWire. “We were trying to find our unique take on that world and how we could be modern and fresh and also sort of pay homage to our own Disney legacy.”

One key way “Hexed” speaks to that Disney tradition is by having a powerful queen who blurs the line between what’s best for her and what’s best for the world. Celeste is also [SPOILER] Alice’s mother and Billie grandmother; there’s a long and proud Disney tradition of very complicated abuelas to outright villain grandmothers, which Bush himself has contributed to in the past.

“The worst part is that my own mother, who’s absolutely lovely, is a grandmother now to my three boys, and she is deeply offended by my choices,” Bush joked to IndieWire about what he has against grandmothers, anyway. “I think the only grandma I’ve written that’s been undeniably loving nonstop is Grandma Tala [from ‘Moana’] — and she didn’t survive the movie.”

But Celeste is a collection of influences from the writers’ lives, the Disney storytelling tradition, and wider pop culture — and not least the actor who ended up voicing her. “We were trying to figure [Celeste] out, and the second that Jodie said yes to the role, it changed the entire character. Because, to be honest, when you’re writing for Jodie Foster, that’s nerve-wracking,” Bush said. “We better get this right. We better make this character interesting and layered.”

Bush and Miller’s writing intended to create space between Celeste’s polished appearance and the roiling jealousy and insecurity she’s buried underneath. “She’s a real villain in a way that’s icky and, for me, that’s a really fun thing to write. On top of the fact that she’s this person trying to take power and maintain power any way that she can, she’s also weirdly vulnerable and needy at the same time. It’s this really uncomfortable combination of characteristics that was really fun to write and to see what Jodie would do with it.”

Leaving space in the writing for animation and performance, the collaboration between story and animation teams is a core part of the writing for “Hexed” and all other Disney Animation Studios films. “We sit down with our story artists and with our animators, and we say, for instance, ‘the premise is we’re going to a weird place with a bunch of reject familiars. What could happen there?’ And everyone spitballs, and great ideas rise to the surface,” Bush said. “More than anything, what I love doing is trying to find a fun sandbox and then being really willing to go wherever the great ideas go.”

Bush, Miller, Veerasunthorn, Trinidad, and Hand all told IndieWire that this openness to great ideas is what makes Disney animation so special, and can make even familiar storytelling territory feel fresh and exciting.

“Maybe we’re coming for granddads next,” Bush said.

I'm not sure which I love more, the main Thanksgiving dinner or all the leftovers I get to enjoy for days afterwards. But one thing I know I don't enjoy is trying to play Tetris in my fridge to make all the food fit.

I've spent years transferring it all into tupperware, trying to make sure they stack safely, but I've always felt like I'm not making the most of my fridge space – until now. I've discovered a space-saving hack that's perfect for the holidays and here's how it works.

A post shared by Laurie (@passionatepennypincher)

On Instagram, Laurie aka @passionatepennypincher shares money-saving tips, meal-planning and practical solutions with her over 400k followers. And it's this space-saving fridge hack that she learnt from her grandma that looks like it could be a game-changer for Thanksgiving leftovers.

Instead of just having one shelf to store food, Laurie creates additional shelves above each pan and dish by using cooling racks to separate them. By placing a cooling rack in-between each layer, you're protecting the dish below from getting squashed, as well as creating a sturdy divide to stack vertically in your fridge.

This two-pack of cooling racks is surprisingly affordable, meaning each one only costs you $4.50. With that, you can create extra shelves in your fridge, as well as having a new place to cool your bakes. Perfect for the holiday season.

Immediately, I can see how this hack will save me money and time by wrapping the tops of pans with foil (or cling wrap) instead of rehoming my leftovers into bulky tupperware. And luckily, I've just bought a bunch of new cooling racks for my holiday baking, but hopefully it's a kitchen staple that most people will already have in their homes.

And while I found it to be an incredibly simple hack, stacking the pans with ease, there are a few things to be aware of. First up, you want to make sure the food is cooled before placing them on top of each other. You also want to stack the heaviest items at the bottom, just to be safe. The cooling racks are sturdy, but it's always a good idea to stack heaviest to lightest.

I also decided that since I was using foil that I'd eventually throw away, I could write on the top of it with pen to mark the date it went into the fridge. I figured if I was doing prep work on my Thanksgiving feast rather than storing leftovers, I could also write the cooking times and temperature on the foil.

#3362. Star Wars' 'The Mandalorian With More Lightsabers' Officially Returns In 2027 & It Changes Everything

Star Wars' Mandalorian-era, lightsaber-filled show returns next year, and it could change everything for the galaxy far, far away. Since its 2019 debut, The Mandalorian has been one of Star Wars' most important stories, not only revitalizing the franchise after the divisive reaction to the sequel trilogy but also exploring a relatively new era of the timeline. Before The Mandalorian, little was known about the New Republic era, despite its crucial placement between the original trilogy and Star Wars: The Force Awakens.

Soon enough, The Mandalorian became more than a show; it became an entire sub-franchise. Alongside the ill-received The Book of Boba Fett, The Mandalorian brought animated Star Wars: The Clone Wars heroes back into the fold, including Mandalorian leader Bo-Katan Kryze and long-lost former Jedi Ahsoka Tano. As Anakin Skywalker's unexpected Padawan, Ahsoka is one of Star Wars' most important characters, a vital player in Anakin's fall to the dark side and the larger Clone Wars conflict.

Ahsoka returned in Star Wars Rebels as an early member of the Rebellion before meeting Din Djarin and the artist formerly known as Baby Yoda in The Mandalorian season 2. Now, Ahsoka has become one of the New Republic era's most influential characters, a genuine threat to the Imperial Remnant. If any character deserves to have a show named after them, it's her.

Disney+'s Ahsoka not only continues The Mandalorian's Imperial Remnant storyline but also picks up where Star Wars Rebels left off, with Ahsoka and Ghost Crew member Sabine Wren setting off on a perilous journey to bring back the exiled Jedi Ezra Bridger. Following The Mandalorian and Grogu's less-than-stellar box office run, Ahsoka's second season, set to debut in January 2027, has the power to change the galaxy and the franchise forever, as returned Imperial mastermind Grand Admiral Thrawn wages war against what remains of the Rebel Alliance.

Ahsoka season 2 will determine Star Wars' future on Disney+ and beyond. Though The Mandalorian has largely been a success, The Mandalorian and Grogu's theatrical failure has thrown the New Republic era's storytelling into question. At Star Wars Celebration 2023, Lucasfilm announced Dave Filoni's Mandalorian-era culmination movie, supposedly meant to bring The Mandalorian, The Book of Boba Fett, and Ahsoka together in one last, Avengers-esque Star Wars-themed hurrah, a version of Timothy Zahn's non-canon Star Wars Legends epic, Heir to the Empire.

Given what happened with The Mandalorian and Grogu and all the other theatrical changes since then — Rey's New Jedi Order movie is still in limbo, with next year's Star Wars: Starfighter taking its place as the first post-Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker story — there's a chance this movie will never come to fruition. Ahsoka season 2 could technically conclude Thrawn's story in its eight-episode run (a pivotal battle between Thrawn and Admiral Ackbar has already been confirmed), setting the stage for the First Order's rise to power as seen in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, bringing the so-called "Mandoverse" to an end once and for all.

However, the Imperial Remnant isn't the only threat in Ahsoka season 2. In fact, Ahsoka and Sabine are in a galaxy even further away than Star Wars' primary galaxy, where a powerful darkness lurks in the shadows, waiting to be unleashed. Ahsoka and Sabine will chase Jedi-turned-mercenary Baylan Skoll across Peridea as he hunts the source of this power, potentially encountering the Star Wars Legends-era Force-wielder Abeloth, otherwise known as the Mother.

Given the Mortis gods' statues (the Father, the Son, and the Daughter) on Peridea and Ahsoka's lasting connection to the Daughter after The Clone Wars' Mortis arc, this seems the most likely path. Abeloth is one of the most powerful figures in the Star Wars Legends continuity, a being of chaos and destruction with the power to bring about the end of "everything."

Ahsoka season 2's first trailer has me very excited about its biggest mystery and the potential debut of one of Star Wars' most powerful villains.

Covering Thrawn's war against the Rebel Alliance and Abeloth's hypothetical re-emergence in eight episodes will be difficult. It'll need to feel like one cohesive whole, especially since both storylines take place in two distinct galaxies. Introducing a villain like Abeloth — or at least someone or something equally powerful — would need to affect the franchise at large. It can't just be a one-and-done event. That makes it feel more likely that the Mandoverse's arc won't end in Ahsoka season 2, though nothing is confirmed.

Ahsoka season 2 is currently the only live-action Star Wars Disney+ show left; no other projects have been officially announced, with the franchise attempting to return to its theatrical roots. Following the Mandoverse, Lucasfilm may benefit from a more balanced approach, investing wisely in both movies and streaming shows that not only expand Star Wars' timeline but also its creative scope. For now, though, Ahsoka season 2 essentially holds the keys to the franchise's future.

Ahsoka season 2 premieres on January 20, 2027, exclusively on Disney+.

#3361. The Perfect Lord of the Rings Cast if It Were Made in 2026

The Lord of the Rings is the most totemic fantasy film franchise of all time. Along with Harry Potter in the 2000s, it precipitated a revival of fantasy cinema that hasn't been matched since. It featured groundbreaking digital effects, incredible sets, miniatures, epic battle sequences, and an emotionally resonant storyline that gave all its technical wizardry purpose. Most of all, the franchise was cast perfectly.

The Lord of the Rings featured a wealth of actors, both seasoned and new, revitalizing the careers of some and launching others. Every actor fit perfectly into their role, and it's hard to imagine anyone else taking them over. But it's 2026, and the internet is the perfect place for wild speculation. While we continue to get new films and series set in J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth, with some roles recast and others played by the same actors, we also can't help but wonder what the original trilogy might have looked like if it were cast right now. If it were, this could be the perfect cast.

When it comes to the iconic villains in The Lord of the Rings, the evil lord Sauron is more of a presence than he is a persona. That leaves most of the acting to his underlings, none more prominent than the sorcerer Saruman. As played by the legendary Sir Christopher Lee in the Peter Jackson films, he exuded power and devilish deception. Any actor taking on the role of Sauron's right-hand wizard would need to have a similar sinister presence, and few can be as intimidating as Ralph Fiennes.

Sure, the English actor is already well known for playing the iconic wizard villain Voldemort in the Harry Potter films, but that shouldn't preclude him from playing another — it's not like Lee hadn't played other supernatural villains before he took on Saruman. Fiennes has a commanding presence, and there's little doubt he'd bring a chilling, distinct energy to the role. No two of his villain performances have ever been the same, and the three-time Oscar-nominated actor has the gravitas to rule Isengard.

Of near equal status to Fiennes and Lee is Sean Bean, an actor who was once best known for always dying on screen. That trend first came to prominence thanks to his role as Boromir, the human member of the Fellowship who fell prey to the temptations of the One Ring before valiantly sacrificing himself. It's a crucial role in The Fellowship of the Ring, requiring an actor who can elicit both sympathy and ire in equal measure.

One does not simply recast a role played by Sean Bean, but in 2026, Theo James seems like he could do well in the role. While he was once pegged for bland leading man roles in franchises like Divergent, James has more recently found more success in roles that operate in grayer moral areas, including his Emmy-nominated turn in The White Lotus and Netflix's The Gentlemen streaming series. He's got the dashing looks of a hero, but the deceitful heart to go along with them, making him the perfect choice for the great warrior from Gondor.

Hotheaded and stubborn but fiercely loyal and honorable, Gimli became a fast fan favorite in the film franchise, mostly thanks to John Rhys-Davies' boisterous performance and his chemistry with Orlando Bloom. Any actor tasked with filling out the dwarven helmet of the character in 2026 would need to be able to recapture that same level of aggressive attitude without becoming abrasive. They'd also need to be able to rock a mean beard. Enter Matt Berry.

Best known to American audiences for his hilarious performance on the vampire series What We Do in the Shadows, Berry has a career of iconic characters to his name in British series such as Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The IT Crowd and Toast of London. He can elicit laughs in how he delivers a single word, and there's no doubt he'd be distinctly different yet just as memorable as Rhys-Davies as everyone's favorite dwarf.

You can't have Gimli without his bromantic elf partner Legolas, a role that made a star out of Orlando Bloom. His ethereal male beauty and soft-spoken delivery made him perfect for the ageless character. While it seems like a role that any pretty blonde boy could be slotted into, there's a deceptive difficulty to the character. Too much personality, and he becomes too human; too much restraint and he becomes a bland bore. It's a fine line that an actor would have to walk, and Jamie Campbell Bower seems like he could walk it.

It might be cheating to include an actor who's already been cast as an elf in The Lord of the Rings, since Bower has been cast as Celeborn for the third season of The Rings of Power, but there's no doubt he'd be on the shortlist for Legolas if the character were being cast in 2026. He's obviously got the look for the character, and his role on Stranger Things showed he can modulate his emotions with quiet intensity. Put him alongside Berry, and a whole new bromance could be born.

Pippin is one half of the second most popular hobbit bromance in The Lord of the Rings. The troublemaker joined Frodo's quest to destroy the One Ring alongside his best friend Merry by mere accident, but he proved his heroism multiple times over across the trilogy. Billy Boyd brought plenty of comic relief to the role, which required a great deal of panicking, and if there's any actor who's recently shown their ability to elicit laughs in the face of danger, it's Austin Abrams.

Abrams broke through last year in Zach Cregger's Weapons as a frazzled drug addict, and he continued his streak of livewire performances this year in both Cregger's new film version of Resident Evil and the survival thriller Whalefall. Abrams can bring levity to even the most bizarre situations, and Pippin finds himself in several of those. Put him in some capri pants and give him some pipe weed, and he'd be right at home in Middle-earth.

Where there's Pippin, you're likely to find Merry, his hobbit compatriot who's maybe just a half step ahead of his friend. Dominic Monaghan had incredible chemistry with Boyd in the films, and the two actors have kept the bromance going outside the franchise, reteaming on stage, on television and co-hosting a podcast together. Abrams would need an equal partner, and Joseph Quinn seems like he could be his perfect Merry.

Quinn has been on an upward trajectory ever since his breakthrough role on Stranger Things, with roles in Marvel movies, horror franchises and an upcoming turn as George Harrison in Sam Mendes' four-part biopic of The Beatles. If he's willing to be "the quiet Beatle," then there's a good chance he'd be the perfect actor to bring out the best in the other hobbits.

If there's one actor who seems irreplaceable in The Lord of the Rings cast, it's Sir Ian McKellen as Gandalf. He's the only actor to have received an Academy Award nomination for his acting in the franchise, and his combination of authority, compassion and wisdom made him as integral to the film as Alec Guinness in Star Wars. McKellen is an acting titan, and it would take another legend to handle the iconic role of Gandalf — Gary Oldman is that legend.

Oldman successfully transitioned from his early character roles into Hollywood's favorite villain for over a decade before becoming a steady mentor in franchises like The Dark Knight and Harry Potter. His added years only make him more suitable for the role now, and he'd bring a wholly different kind of wisdom to the role. If there's any actor who could command the same level of respect as McKellen in the role, it's Oldman.

Of all the members of the original Fellowship, Aragorn is the only one who already has a new actor cast in the role in 2026. Jamie Dornan was recently announced to take over the role from original actor Viggo Mortensen for the upcoming The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum. While it remains to be seen whether Dornan is able to acquit himself in the role and emerge from the shadow of Mortensen's star-making turn, there's no harm in suggesting another actor who might have also been a suitable fit for the role.

Henry Cavill came on the scene as Zack Snyder's Man of Steel, and while the DC superhero franchise didn't give Cavill enough room to fly, he's proven his chops as a leading man elsewhere, and shown he knows how to swing a sword in The Witcher. With a little more salt added to his pepper, Cavill has the right amount of maturity to take on the role of the once and future king of Gondor, and would be more than adept at the requisite action scenes.

The most loyal of all hobbits, Samwise Gamgee is one of the most likable fantasy movie heroes of all time. His unwavering loyalty to Frodo is matched only by his love of potatoes. The bond between the two hobbits formed the emotional backbone of the entire trilogy, and a great deal of that was due to the warmth that Sean Astin brought to the role. Any actor cast in the role now would need to be able to elicit the same amount of sympathy and likability. Fortunately, there's an actor who's already done that with another fantasy character named Sam.

John Bradley is best known for his role as Samwell Tarly on Game of Thrones, a character who shares more than a few traits with Samwise. It might seem like lazy casting, but sometimes an actor is simply built for a certain kind of role, and Bradley fits the bill for Sam. He has warmth and likability, and if he were cast as Samwise, he'd get to be more heroic, since one notably different trait of Tarwell was his cowardice. Casting Bradley as Frodo's faithful companion would be the perfect opportunity for him to be a hero.

It's the most important role in the entire trilogy. Frodo Baggins has the heaviest cross, or ring, to bear of any member of the Fellowship, and his suffering could easily become unbearable to watch if played by the wrong actor. Elijah Wood weaponized his innocent, youthful looks to really drive home how harrowed the character became over his journey, balancing the moments where the character is sympathetic and just plain pathetic. In 2026, there's one actor who could find that same level of innocence more perfectly than any other.

Josh O'Connor may have lost the role of James Bond, but it's arguable he's more suited to Hobbiton than Her Majesty's Secret Service. He's risen through the ranks in Hollywood thanks to his starring roles in films like Wake Up, Dead Man and Disclosure Day, both of which relied on his soft-spoken charm to play men who found themselves in over their heads. If that's not perfect for Frodo, then who is in 2026?

Meanwhile, the already-popular Disney+/Hulu bundle is now $4.99 (was $11.99), and for those looking to spend as little as possible, Paramount+ Premium has dropped to $2.99. And these are just the start of the streaming deals.

I'm rounding up all the best Black Friday streaming deals today (Nov. 26), so you can enjoy vast libraries of movies and TV shows without your monthly entertainment bill spiralling out of control. Plus, I'll highlight any new deals as they go live.

The Disney+ and Hulu bundle is a solid savings all year long, but for Black Friday, it's an even bigger bargain at $4.99. For less than $5 a month, you get two streaming services, offering the best of Disney, Marvel and Star Wars, alongside Hulu's excellent library of more grown-up content. Even better, if you lock in this discounted price today, you'll get Disney+ and Hulu at almost 60% off for a full 12 months.

Paramount+ has discounted every tier to $2.99, so the choice is obvious: get Paramount+ Premium. With this top-tier package, you get full access to the Paramount+ library with ad-free streaming, Showtime originals, and your local CBS station. There's plenty to watch, from the final season of "Yellowjackets" to live sports, like NFL and Champions League soccer. The only downside is that this offer is only valid for 2 months, which feels stingy compared to rivals.

Apple TV is a streaming service you shouldn't overlook. It packs one of the best original libraries of any streamer, with a wealth of must-watch TV shows you can't find anywhere else. Ahead of Black Friday, Apple TV is 50% off, giving you six months of access for $6.99 a month. That's enough time to binge a wide selection of the very best Apple TV Originals from "Severance" to "Slow Horses".

HBO Max is offering 50% off its Basic with Ads plan. Half price on our favorite streaming service is a deal we're eager to shout about. HBO Max offers a near-unbeatable library with top-tier television and plenty of blockbuster movies. Sweetening the deal, the discounted price lasts for 12 months, so you can stream the best of HBO Max for an entire year. Get it now ahead of "Harry Potter" season 1 arriving in December.

Peacock skipped Black Friday last year, but has returned with a respectable discount for 2026. It's not the most headline-grabbing saving at 31%, but plans start from $2.99 per month for the Select tier. However, I recommend the Premium tier for $8.99, which gives you access to the full Peacock library, including shows, movies, live sports, and Peacock Originals.

Horror fans, this one's worth a look. You can currently add MGM+ to your Prime Video subscription for just $1.99 per month for two months, down from $7.99, saving 75%. It's home to brilliant originals like "From" and "The Institute," plus a great selection of movies, including "Project Hail Mary."

Prime Video add-on subscriptions: deals from $0.99Prime Video add-on subscriptions offer some of the cheapest Black Friday streaming deals of the season. Discounts start from $0.99 and include Paramount+, Apple TV, HBO Max, Starz, AMC+, MGM+, BritBox and Hallmark+. Upgrade your Prime Video library with these great deals.

Sadly, there isn't a YouTube Premium Black Friday deal (at least, not yet).

As a longtime YouTube Premium user, I'd love a good deal, but unfortunately, YouTube doesn't seem interested in offering one. Perhaps the service is already popular enough that Google doesn't feel it needs a Black Friday push.

If you're a fan of British TV and don't normally have access to it, a BritBox subscription might be for you. Right now, you can jump in and give it a shot for $2.99 a month for the first two months. After that, the price jumps to $10.99 per month, which is still reasonable for the quantity of content on offer ("Downton Abbey," "Death In Paradise," "Vera," "Father Brown", "Ludwig" and many more).

While most of the focus has been on streaming subscriptions, there are some great deals on Prime for individual movies.

Okay, maybe not all of the deals, but you can get a lot of streaming deals through Amazon Prime Video.

HBO Max, BritBox, Apple TV, AMC+, Crunchyroll, and many others are available through Amazon at sizable discounts. Some are even 70% off!

With all this streaming content on sale, let's not neglect the streaming hardware. I think the best deals right now are on Amazon's Fire Stick devices, which are $15 for the HD version and $19 for the 4K version.

Amazon’s new 4K entry pairs ultra-Vega OS software with direct TV USB power and a redesigned tactile remote you can actually navigate in the dark. It's one of the best value options for 4K streaming with this discount.

I really like Apple TV because it has "Stick." I keep telling everyone that the show is solid, even if you don't care about golf.

"Stick" might not be perfect, but it's a fun show overall, and I'll watch most of Owen Wilson's movies and shows with great joy.

Now that season 2 of "Stick" has hit the streaming service, and with the Black Friday deal getting you Apple TV for $6.99 per month, it's the perfect time to binge both seasons.

In case you need a quick recap (and you skipped the one above), here are all of the best deals running right now:

It's not an exhaustive list of streaming deals, but it covers the big ones.

There's one streaming service that's taking more money off its normal price than any other: Frndly TV. You can take an impressive 92% off the normal price — 3 months for just $.99/month. You'd normally need to pay $12.99 for the service, so it's a ridiculous deal.

Of course, you might not have heard of Frndly TV, and you wouldn't be alone there. The service offers Hallmark movies, mysteries, classic TV, westerns, game shows and more.

Gems like "Good Boy," "Tales From the Crypt," "Caveat," and all kinds of big-name classics are on the service, and you can watch them all without breaking the bank.

When you see something listed as 79% off, it sounds like a fake deal. And a lot of the time, it is.

But in the case of Paramount+, you can legitimately save 79% off the regular price for Black Friday. It's one of the more underrated streaming services in my opinion, so don't snooze on this deal.

I signed up for this one the moment I saw it go live. The Disney+/Hulu bundle for $4.99/month is a fantastic bargain.

You get a full year at that price, which breaks down to about $60 total. That's a lot of streaming content for a little bit of money.

Are you a football fan looking forward to watching the big Thanksgiving games today? Are you going to sit back and watch some movies? Maybe you're more of a show binger.

Whatever the case, there are streaming deals available on the services you want that'll let you watch everything!

Here are 4 of my favorite deals you can get today:

Let's be real: Black Friday is throwing a lot of streaming deals at us, but most of us don't have endless cash. Even at discounted prices, signing up for every service under the sun adds up quickly. So if you're only going to grab a few bargains this year, I'd prioritize these three.

First up is HBO Max for $5.49/month through Prime Video Channels, down from $10.99. That price is locked in for 12 months, so you can stream the next seasons of "The Pitt," "The Last of Us" and "The White Lotus" for less.

Next, I'd snag Apple TV for $6.99/month for six months, down from $14.99. While Apple TV doesn't boast as huge of a library as other streamers, it makes up the lack of quantity with very high quality. Finally, there's the Disney+ and Hulu bundle for $4.99/month for 12 months, down from $11.99. That's nearly 60% off two services, with everything from Marvel and Star Wars to Hulu's excellent grown-up TV lineup, like "Only Murders in the Building."

Grab all three and you'll pay just $17.47/month, instead of the regular combined price of $37.97. That's savings of about 54%, or more than $20 a month. Not bad for three of the best streaming libraries around. Now that's a Black Friday haul I can get behind.

Thanksgiving isn't complete without a little Charlie Brown. Snoopy's popcorn-and-jellybean feast is as much a holiday tradition as the actual turkey.

If you want to revisit "A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving" today, you'll find it streaming exclusively on Apple TV. And there's a pretty sweet Black Friday bonus: You can get six months of Apple TV for just $6.99/month, down from $14.99. That's a 53% saving and plenty of time to catch up on the Peanuts gang's other holiday specials, including "A Charlie Brown Christmas."

Netflix is famously allergic to discounts. The streamer has never really played the Black Friday game, so don't hold your breath waiting for a half-price subscription. But I do have a little workaround: T-Mobile. The wireless carrier is rolling out a bunch of Black Friday promotions, and some of its revamped T-Mix plans let you pick Netflix as a free perk. It's a clever way to get your Netflix fix without paying for another standalone subscription, especially if you're already considering switching wireless providers.

And T-Mobile has some tempting family-plan pricing, too. You can get four lines for $100/month, or about $25 per line, which is worth a look if your current wireless bill is getting out of hand. The catch is that Netflix isn't included with every plan, so you'll want to check which T-Mix tier and T-Mobile Picks you're eligible for before signing up.

Consider this a backdoor Black Friday streaming deal for anyone who refuses to pay full price for Netflix.

Streaming should be making our lives easier, but sometimes it feels like a part-time job just keeping up with it all. Between ever-increasing subscription prices, shows taking approximately 47 years to return, beloved series getting canceled before their time and spending half the night scrolling without finding anything to watch, there's plenty to complain about.

So I'm curious: What's your biggest streaming frustration right now? Cast your vote in the poll below!

Happy Thanksgiving! If there's one movie that belongs on your holiday watchlist, it's "Planes, Trains and Automobiles." Steve Martin and John Candy's misadventure in getting home for Thanksgiving is still one of the funniest, most heartwarming holiday movies ever made. It's also painfully relatable if you've ever tried traveling during the holiday rush.

You can stream it on Paramount+, which has a Black Friday deal that makes a last-minute subscription very tempting: Every tier is just $2.99/month for two months, including Premium.

I'd go straight for Premium, which gets you the full Paramount+ library with ad-free streaming, Showtime originals and your local CBS station. There's plenty more to enjoy beyond the Thanksgiving laughs, including the final season of "Yellowjackets," NFL games and Champions League soccer.

I'm so excited about Netflix's upcoming "Pride and Prejudice" series, because apparently I'll never tire of watching Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy fall in love. If you're counting down the days, now's a perfect time to revisit some of the most beloved adaptations of Jane Austen's novel.

The iconic 1995 BBC miniseries starring Colin Firth and the 1980 version are both streaming on BritBox, which is currently just $2.75/month through Prime Video, down from $10.99. Meanwhile, the 2005 movie with Keira Knightley and Matthew Macfadyen is on Peacock, where Black Friday plans start at just $2.99/month.

Whether you're Team Colin Firth or Team Matthew Macfadyen, these deals make it easy to get your Austen fix without spending a fortune. Now, excuse me while I impatiently wait for a new Mr. Darcy to grace my screen.

With "Avengers: Doomsday" arriving in just a few weeks, there's no better time to brush up on your Marvel Cinematic Universe homework. Whether you need to revisit the Infinity Saga or catch up on the newer movies, Disney+ has you covered. And right now, you can get Disney+ and Hulu together for just $4.99/month for 12 months, down from $11.99. That's nearly 60% off for an entire year!

For less than the price of a fancy coffee, you're getting two streaming services packed with entertainment. Disney+ brings you the Marvel movies, Star Wars and all your Disney favorites, while Hulu serves up a more grown-up mix of acclaimed shows and movies. Consider this your invitation to clear your schedule, fire up that MCU marathon and get ready for "Doomsday."

Between price hikes, password crackdowns and yet another must-watch show landing on a different platform, keeping up with streaming subscriptions is practically a part-time job. And with all the Black Friday deals tempting us to sign up for even more, I'm curious: How many streaming services are you currently paying for?

Are you keeping it lean with one or two, or have you lost count somewhere around seven? No judgment here. (Well, maybe a little.) Vote in the poll below!

I have a bone to pick with everyone who slept on "A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms." Maybe it got overshadowed by the dragon-sized expectations of "House of the Dragon," but Dunk and Egg's scrappy little Westeros adventure is an absolute delight. It's funny, heartfelt and refreshingly unpretentious for a "Game of Thrones" spinoff. I'm starting to put together my best TV shows of the year list, and you better believe "Knight" is getting a spot. If you haven't watched yet, HBO Max is just $5.49/month through Prime Video Channels for 12 months, down from $10.99.

That's 50% off a full year of one of streaming's best libraries, packed with prestige TV, blockbuster movies and plenty of binge-worthy originals. And with the new "Harry Potter" arriving in December and the next season of "The Pitt" in January, there's even more reason to sign up.

I'm a huge "Slow Horses" fan, and if you've somehow missed this gloriously dysfunctional crew of MI5 misfits, Apple's Black Friday deal is your chance to fix that. Apple TV is down to just $6.99/month for six months, saving you 53% off its regular $14.99 price.

That's more than enough time to binge Jackson Lamb's messy band of spies, whose botched assignments and sharp banter make"Slow Horses" one of my favorite shows on TV.

Of course, "Slow Horses" isn't the only reason to grab this deal. Apple TV has a stacked originals lineup, including "Severance," "Silo" and plenty more titles (some not even starting with the letter "S") worth adding to your watchlist.

It's beginning to look a lot like Hallmark Christmas! If you're already dreaming of snowy small towns, cozy fireplaces, handsome strangers and a little festive romance, Hallmark+ is the streaming service for you. It's basically Christmas all year round, with a huge collection of feel-good holiday movies that'll have you reaching for the hot chocolate and putting your decorations up early.

Whether you're after a cheesy Christmas rom-com or a heartwarming festive favorite, consider this your sign to get merry and start streaming. After all, there's snow place like Hallmark for Christmas movies!

As a horror nerd, I'm always on the lookout for my next nightmare-inducing watch, and two streaming services I think deserve a spot on your subscription list are HBO Max and Peacock. Both have a seriously tempting selection of scary flicks, from supernatural chiller "The Conjuring "and the blood-soaked thrills of "Evil Dead Rise" on HBO Max to genre classics like "The Texas Chain Saw Massacre" and "Night of the Living Dead" on Peacock.

HBO Max is also home to newer horror favorites like "Weapons," "Sinners" and "Bring Her Back," while Peacock has plenty to explore if you're after slashers, creature features or something a little more psychological. Whether you're a seasoned horror fan or just looking for something to scare you silly this weekend, I'd definitely give these two platforms a closer look.

Subscribing to streaming services through Prime Video can be a convenient way to keep all your entertainment in one place, particularly if you regularly switch between platforms. Prime Video Channels lets you add services such as MGM+, Paramount+, Starz and Crunchyroll directly to your Amazon account, so you can browse and watch their content without jumping between different apps.

If you've been meaning to explore more anime, now is a brilliant time to give Crunchyroll a try! It's home to one of the biggest anime libraries around, with everything from long-running favorites like "One Piece" to newer hits such as "Dan Da Dan" and "Jujutsu Kaisen." Whether you're a longtime anime fan or a complete newcomer, there's plenty to get stuck into. With a Black Friday discount on its Fan subscription, you can explore the library without paying full price!

We've talked a lot about the Disney+/Hulu bundle, but it's not the only great bundle deal for Black Friday. Prime Video's add-on subscription sale offers an AMC+ and MGM+ bundle for $3.49 per month for 2 months (was $13.99). Giving you a pair of solid streamers for a single, pretty low monthly fee. Between the two, there are plenty of worthwhile TV shows and movies to watch. Might I recommend "The Vampire Lestat" (pictured above) from AMC+? I've not watched it myself, but my colleagues recommend it very highly, and it's rated 96% on Rotten Tomatoes.

One of my favorite sitcoms of all time returned last year, and to my delight it's a rare revival that's actually pretty great. I'm of course talking about "Scrubs," the second season of the reboot is currently airing on Hulu, so if you want something to watch after scoring the Disney+/Hulu bundle for $4.99, the new "Scrubs" is a worthy pick.

One of the best streaming deals right now actually comes through Walmart+, the retailer's rival to Amazon Prime comes with a host of perks, including the choice of Paramount+ or Peacock at no additional cost. Plus, right now, you can try Walmart+ for $1 for 30 days, giving you all the perks for a month, including free delivery ($35 minimum spend), which is useful if you're shopping Walmart's Black Friday sale.

The elephant in the room right now is where are all the Netflix Black Friday deal? Well, here's the bad news, there is very little chance of any Netflix deals this week. With its position as the world's biggest streamer secured, Netflix rarely, if ever, offers discounts and deals. In my entire time covering Black Friday professionally, I've never seen a Netflix Black Friday deal, and 2026 is looking like no exception to that trend.

One important tip before you sign up: don't forget to cancel! Many of these Black Friday streaming offers are introductory discounts, meaning your subscription will automatically renew at the standard monthly price once the promotional period ends.

I'd recommend setting a reminder on your phone for a few days before your deal expires, so you have time to decide whether you want to keep the service or move on. You can usually cancel at any time without losing access to the discounted subscription period you've already paid for. Trust me, the last thing you want is a surprise streaming bill a few months down the line!

With so many streaming services competing for your attention, keeping subscriptions to all of them year-round can get expensive pretty quickly. That’s why I'm a big fan of rotating streaming subscriptions rather than paying for everything at once.

Instead of juggling Hulu, Disney+, Paramount+, Peacock and the rest every month, I’d pick one or two services, catch up on the shows and movies I’ve been meaning to watch, then cancel and move on to another platform. With plenty of streaming services offering monthly plans and regular new releases, there’s little reason to pay for a library you’re not actively using. And there’s no better time to cancel and make the most out of these Black Friday discounts.

Our streaming editor, Kelly Woo, said in her guide that she prefers to “play musical subscriptions instead: Cancel the ones I'm not using, hop back in when a sale comes along.”

There’s plenty of fresh entertainment arriving this weekend if you’re looking to make the most of your Black Friday streaming subscriptions. Disney+ has a couple of family-friendly treats, including “Mickey's Home Alone” and the new movie “Dasher,” while “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” season 3 also continues with new episodes.

Over on Hulu, you can catch the new action thriller “Runner,” starring Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson. HBO Max is bringing fantasy adventure “The Magic Faraway Tree,” while Paramount+ has some festive fun lined up with “SpongeBob SquarePants: Merry Christmas, Mr. Plankton” and horror-comedy “On the Last Day of Christmas.”

There’s also “Shop What Happens,” a new Peacock original if you’re after something different this weekend.

If there's one reason to grab this MGM+ Black Friday deal, it's "From." Seriously, I cannot recommend this show enough. It's one of my absolute favorite horror series, and if you love a good mystery with plenty of creepy twists, terrifying creatures and unanswered questions, you're in for a treat.

I've been hooked since season 1, and it's the kind of show that leaves you thinking. With four seasons available to binge (and season 5 on the way), there's plenty to keep you occupied, too. You can currently add MGM+ to your Prime Video subscription for just $1.99 per month for two months. That's a pretty easy yes from me, especially if you've somehow managed to avoid the residents of this very strange town until now!

Lionsgate+ is a real treasure trove of great movies from major favorites like "La La Land," "Knives Out," and "The Hunger Games" to some overlooked gems like "The Peanut Butter Falcon" and "Killing Them Softly." There are loads of worthwhile flicks to enjoy, and you can add Lionsgate+ to Prime Video for just $1.75/month in this Black Friday deal. Though it only runs for two months, so you'll need to cram in some movie marathons before being stung by a price hike after the discount period.

BritBox brings "the best of British TV" to viewers in the United States, and while as a U.K. native I might slightly disagree with that marketing hook, the platform does offer plenty of great TV directly from the United Kingdom. This includes Original series like "Death Valley" and "Ludwig" (pictured above). You can add BritBox to your Prime Video account for just $2.75 a month for two months, down from $10.99.

It's not just streaming services discounted for Black Friday, the seasonal shopping event also brings discounts on streaming accessories, in this case a range of Amazon Fire TV Sticks, from the basic HD basic to the premium Fire TV Cube (which, I guess isn't technically a streaming stick). After all, there's no point scoring a big saving on a great streaming service, if you don't have the necessary equipment to stream at home.

Over on HBO Max, you watch every chapter of the "Game of Thrones" saga, that's the complete run of the original show, alongside its two spin-offs, "House of the Dragon" and "A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms." Just to remind you, if you'd not seen my several other mentions, HBO Max is $5.49 a month for a full year, more than enough time to tear through every twist, turn and betrayal in these Westeros-set TV shows.

Check out this low-priced deal: Frndly TV is $0.99 per month, a huge saving compared to its regular $12.99 monthly fee. The platform gives you access to live TV channels like Hallmark, A&E, History, Lifetime, The Weather Channel, and a more. Plus, there's an "On Demand" library, if you want to catch up on anything you miss.

The Tom's Guide team loves "Slow Horses." This Apple Original spy thriller series is a rarity in the current streaming landscape, having debuted a new season every year since 2022. It just wrapped up its sixth season in October, and the quality hasn't dipped. Grab Apple TV for $6.99/month right now, and go binge "Slow Horses."

Most streaming deals offer a discounted monthly price, but how about an entire streaming service for a full year for a single fee? That's the offer from Starz, which has discounted its annual plan down to just $11.99. A massive discount from its usual $69.99 price, and once you sign up, you can enjoy a full year of movies like "Michael," "Power Ballad," and "In the Grey" alongside shows like "Sweetpea" season 2. This deal comes as part of the Prime Video add-on subscription sale.

"Avengers: Doomsday" is on the horizon, so if you want to catch up on the MCU, or circle back to any chapters you'd skipped, then Disney+ has the entire saga to date streaming (not excluding the Sony Spider-Man movies). You can get Disney+ bundled with Hulu for 4.99 for a full year thanks to this top-rated Black Friday deal.

"The Office" is one of the most popular comfort-watch shows around; fans will watch it on repeat endlessly, and if you're looking to head to Scranton, Peacock is the place to be. The streamer offers all 9 seasons (that's 201 episodes), alongside exclusive "Superfan Episodes" with deleted and extended scenes. You can get Peacock Select right now for $2.99, which includes "The Office." However, if you want to watch those "Superfan Episodes," you'll need Premium, as they're classed as Peacock Originals.

Christmas is a month away, so now is the time to be streaming all manner of Hallmark movies, because no network churns out as many festive-themed flicks as Hallmark. Thanks to this Prime Video add-on subscription deal, you can get access to Hallmark+ for just $2.25/month. This deal runs for 3 months, which is more than enough time to cram in dozens of Hallmark Original holiday movies this season.

I'll confess to being less of an anime expert, but I do know one thing "Chainsaw Man" is an epic series, and well-worth watching. You can stream the 12-episode first season and the also-excellent movie, "Reze Arc," on Crunchyroll, a streaming service dedicated to all thing anime. Even better, you can sign up for just $3.99 right now.

"South Park" has been airing since 1997, and with 29 seasons and 343 episodes (and counting), that's a lot of crass animated humor to enjoy. Paramount+ is the streaming home of the iconic series, and you can sign up to Paramount+ Premium for just $2.99 (for two months) thanks to this Black Friday deal. Get the deal, and then start binging some classic episodes of "South Park."

If the Prime Video library wasn't already big enough for you, then check out these add-on subscription deals, which let you access entire additional services within the Prime Video UI. We're not talking low grade libraries either, there's Apple TV, Paramount+, Starz, MGM+. AMC+, Hallmark+, Crunchyroll and plenty more to pick from, and with deals starting at $0.99, some of these add-ons are great value.

To my great surprise, this year's "Minions and Monsters" is an excellent family movie, with slapstick comedy that the little ones will love, and some genuinely great references to classic cinema. It's streaming over on Peacock, and you can get the streaming service for $8.99 in this Black Friday deal. The platform also houses the rest of the Minions adventure, but in my opinion, the latest one is clearly the best.

"The Invite" is one of the year's best movies. A ridiculously well-written dramedy with an excellent cast, it's funny, it's clever and just the right amount of tragic. It's also streaming on HBO Max, and with rumors of Oscar noms in its future, grab this Black Friday deal on the streaming service and give "The Invite" a watch, it's brilliant.

Forget Ted Lasso, the best feel-good watch on Apple TV is "Trying," this easy-going British comedy about adoption concluded its fifth season over the summer, and it's like a warm hug in TV show form. Give it a watch to chase off the winter blues, and with this Black Friday Apple TV deal you have no excuse not to try out "Trying".

The Disney+/Hulu bundle is one I'd recommend at full price; $11.99 for two great streaming services represents good value for money. For Black Friday, you can score the same bundle for $4.99, which is excellent value. One of my favorite things about this deal is that it runs for 12 months, so you get a year of both for just $5 a month.

Good morning (and a Happy Thanksgiving)! It's Black Friday Eve, but there's no need to wait until tomorrow to start shopping for streaming discounts, but plenty of the biggest streamers around have already started offering massive savings, and I'm here to bring you all the best Black Friday streaming deals that you can score now.

#3359. CarPlay Ultra coming to these cars, according to Apple

Last year, Apple officially announced CarPlay Ultra, the next-generation version of CarPlay that it first teased way back at WWDC 2022.

CarPlay Ultra first launched for Aston Martin owners in the United States and Canada. What about other automakers? Here’s what we know.

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Updated November 24, 2026: Latest on Hyundai, more.

In December 2023, Apple said that Porsche and Aston Martin would be the first automakers to support next-generation CarPlay starting in 2024. That deadline came and went, and Apple confirmed in January that next-gen CarPlay had been delayed but was still in development.

Apple doesn’t offer a timeline on when CarPlay Ultra will actually be available through any other brand beyond Aston Martin. The company also does not have a dedicated list of automakers that have signed on to support CarPlay Ultra listed on its website.

When Apple announced the next-generation version of CarPlay at WWDC 2022, however, it stated that several brands had committed to supporting the platform. In May of last year, Apple touted that three new partners had signed on: Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis.

However, several brands have also dropped their plans to support CarPlay Ultra. Mercedes-Benz was originally on Apple’s list, but abandoned its plans to support next-generation CarPlay in 2024. According to the Financial Times, Audi, Volvo, Polestar, and Renault have also decided against supporting CarPlay Ultra, despite originally being touted as partners by Apple.

With all of that said, here is the full list of automakers who plan to eventually support CarPlay Ultra, as of November 2026.

What do we know beyond this list? Not a whole lot. Interestingly, Top Gear reported that the Hyundai IONIQ 3 EV would support CarPlay Ultra. Hyundai announced the IONIQ 3 in April, but has not commented on whether the vehicle will support CarPlay Ultra as rumors suggested.

Mark Gurman at Bloomberg has also reported CarPlay Ultra will launch for “least one major new Hyundai/Kia model in the second half of this year.”

While Apple has touted Ford as a partner for CarPlay Ultra, the automaker recently signaled it’s not too impressed with the first version of a platform.

In a recent interview, Ford CEO Jim Farley was asked whether the company is “considering” CarPlay Ultra support. Here’s what he said:

“We are. We don’t like the execution in round 1 of Ultra, but we’re very committed to Apple. I’ve talked to Tim many times about this.”

It’s better than a flat “no,” but perhaps not the enthusiasm Ford drivers might have hoped to hear.

The question at this point is whether any other automakers have ditched CarPlay Ultra. Ideally, Apple will provide a full list sooner rather than later, but in the meantime, this is the only information we have.

Learn more about everything new with CarPlay Ultra in our dedicated coverage.

The 9-1-1 franchise returned for its second year with two shows on ABC's schedule. The flagship series is in its tenth season, which featured a massive volcano in Los Angeles in its first several episodes. Meanwhile, the second offshoot, 9-1-1: Nashville, introduced a new character, Rogue (Ryan Phillippe), just as Nashville came under threat from a killer called the Pharaoh (A.J. Buckley). Both shows are now on hiatus until next year, and ABC has already set return dates.

When the franchise returns, each show will focus on its own storylines. 9-1-1 signed off with a massive cliffhanger that saw Athena (Angela Bassett) pass out while being interviewed. It is unclear what is wrong with her, and the show will explore that in two episodes. Could it have something to do with being underground during the volcano? The event has left some injuries whose symptoms have yet to show up for characters like Harry, who watched someone die. Meanwhile, 9-1-1: Nashville also closed out with danger as the Pharaoh targeted Don (Chris O'Donnell) and Rogue for being firstborn sons.

When the shows return on Thursday, January 7, and resolve these hanging storylines, fans can also expect a crossover. 9-1-1 showrunner Tim Minear confirmed that the story originates in 9-1-1: Nashville. The spin-off's showrunner, Rashad Raisani, also confirmed that the crossover will introduce one of Rogue's sons, who will appear in the LA crossover with 9-1-1. "We want to let people know that these people have lives off the few minutes of screen time they get in an episode, that they do have rich backstories and lives, and we will be bringing them in," Raisani told Collider. Meanwhile, ABC has also unveiled its winter schedule.

The Rookie started as a show about a man starting over at forty-five and turned into a proper ensemble drama somewhere around season three. Here is which of them you are, and the case for yours being the best of the four.

You started late and you are not embarrassed about it. Nolan walks into the academy at forty-five surrounded by people half his age, and the show is honest that this is both his biggest disadvantage and the only reason he is any good at the job.

You are better at this than people expect and you intend to keep proving it. Chen goes from rookie to the best undercover officer in the division, which works because she is genuinely good at becoming somebody else and genuinely bad at pretending she does not care.

You are hard on people because you have decided that is what caring looks like. Bradford is introduced as the worst training officer in the building and slowly revealed as the one who takes the job most seriously, which are the same fact seen from two angles.

You said what you wanted and then you went and got it. Lopez wanted detective from the first episode, said so out loud, and got there by being better at the work than the people who were quieter about wanting it.
