30 years later, 'The Birdcage' remains the ultimate survival guide for chaotic holiday dinner-table drama

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Deck the halls with family drama … fa-la-la-la-awkward. You don’t need Thanksgiving to start an argument at the dinner table, though it is the ultimate excuse to air every grievance you’ve suppressed since that doomed New Year’s resolution to "be more zen." (Spoiler alert: It didn’t stick.)

“The Birdcage” came out in 1996, yet 30 years later, it couldn’t be more relatable. Sure, it isn't marketed as a Thanksgiving movie, nor does it take place during the holiday. Still, the Robin Williams classic centers on a high-stakes family dinner showdown, serving sus soup — and plenty of political in-law drama — in bowls decked out with naked men. That kind of spice puts memaw’s pumpkin pie to shame.

The Mike Nichols-directed film is certainly a product of its time, yet nearly a decade before “Brokeback Mountain,” it did far more for LGBTQ+ inclusivity than the infamous cowboy flick.

The premise of “The Birdcage” sounds like an alpha-male podcaster’s worst nightmare: What happens when the not-so-demure daughter of a right-wing politician marries the son of a gay cabaret owner and his drag queen partner?

There’s meeting the parents, and then there’s meeting your future son-in-law’s dad and his "wife" — who happens to be Albert in drag. Robin Williams anchors the film as doting dad Armand, while Nathan Lane plays Albert, his longtime partner. Their on-screen dynamic swings from heartfelt and wholesome to wildly theatrical without ever tipping into pure parody. Dan Futterman also brings an exasperated charm to Armand’s son, groom-to-be Val — no small feat for a guy asking his dad to step back into the closet to appease his future in-laws. Not cool, Val.

The "meet the parents" trope wasn't exactly fresh in ’96; the movie was adapted from Jean Poiret’s 1973 play, “La Cage aux Folles.” Yet Gene Hackman as ultra-conservative Senator Keeley, Dianne Wiest as his wife Louise, and Calista Flockhart as bride-to-be Barbara bring an unexpected edge to a rocky family dynamic (featuring some mild repression). Even Hank Azaria (Agador) and Christine Baranski (Katharine) steal every scene they’re in. The best part? Vocally homophobic Senator Keeley seems to have a bit of a thing for Albert in a wig. Who’s going to tell him?

Beneath the farce and political clash sits a relatable story about identity, loyalty and fighting for love that hits hard during Thanksgiving and the endless gauntlet of holiday obligations that follow. Even if you think the Goldmans are way too lenient on the Keeleys (yeah, hi), it’s always easier to watch someone else’s family meltdown than to survive your own.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

You can certainly argue that “The Birdcage” isn’t perfect. It leans a little too heavily into femme stereotypes, traditional gender roles and "let's just agree to disagree" diplomacy at the queer characters' expense. Three decades on, though, it still feels like a movie that celebrates the queer community rather than treating us as the punchline, which is more than I can say for prestige dramas like “Brokeback Mountain” that double down on queer tragedy and shame. I usually champion queer stories led by creatives from the community, yet “The Birdcage” used its star-studded cast to pull mainstream audiences into an early, unapologetic celebration of queer joy.

What you take away from the movie ultimately depends on what you need. If it offers a blueprint for surviving clashing ideologies without a Thanksgiving panic attack, great. Personally, I see it as a reminder to love yourself loudly, regardless of who’s sitting across the table. Sister Sledge’s "We Are Family" plays throughout the film, but being family doesn't mean tolerating prejudice — it’s about championing a second, more vital bond: found family.

So, whether you put it on after dinner to scandalize Aunt Carol’s delicate sensibilities, or skip the family gathering altogether and protect your peace, “The Birdcage” is the exact antidote you need when you're dreading a family showdown before anyone even says grace.

#3355. 12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

This series will help you pick the perfect presents, decor, and activities to make this Christmas the Best Christmas Ever.

In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

As for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting new movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:

Go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

Pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

Get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

Hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

Shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should plan ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you plan to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

The most important advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

#3354. Donald Trump Blasts 'Lowlife' New York Times Reporter in Late Night Thanksgiving Rant

Donald Trump is kicking off Thanksgiving by carving up a New York Times reporter ... unleashing a late-night rant against the journalist before most Americans even got their turkeys in the oven.

POTUS took to Truth Social at around 1 AM Thursday ... going off on veteran journalist David E. Sanger over an article examining a short-lived stock market rally involving tech giant Nvidia.

Trump accused Sanger of conveniently leaving out what he considers some of his administration's biggest accomplishments ... rattling off everything from border security and crime rates to tax cuts and military victories.

But Trump quickly made things personal, writing ... "David Sanger is a lowlife that only writes what he is told to write by his bosses."

The president also managed to drag former President Barack Obama into his Thanksgiving tirade ... blaming his predecessor for a situation involving unstable explosives in Iowa that the Army recently detonated.

For some context ... Sanger has been with the Times for more than 4 decades and has been part of 3 Pulitzer Prize-winning reporting teams.

Trump wrapped up his post by boasting about his record on the world stage and the country's standing internationally.

So much for a quiet Thanksgiving morning!!!

#3352. Apple Home accessories: Here are my five top picks for your smart home

Apple Home is kicking off a new era with Siri AI-driven products like HomeView, making it a great time to upgrade your smart home with Apple Home-compatible accessories. Here are my top five picks.

iOS 27 upgraded Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video service (included with iCloud+) in several key ways. You’ll now get searchable videos, highlighted clips, 4K support, and more.

I have two recommendations for HomeKit Secure Video-compatible cameras. The main difference is video quality, and whether they’re designed for outdoor use or only indoors.

Smart locks have always offered convenience, but with the advent of Ultra Wideband-supported locks, they’re better than ever.

Aqara’s U400 smart lock was among the first to introduce Ultra Wideband, which enables your door to lock and unlock automatically when it senses your presence. Unlike prior smart lock automations that relied on Bluetooth, Ultra Wideband offers excellent reliability and precision for a great overall experience.

Want to open your garage door with a quick Siri command, or via CarPlay or the Home app on iPhone? Smart garage door openers with Apple Home support can deliver that, and my recommendation is the meross MSG150HK.

meross says the MSG150HK is compatible with “the vast majority of Chamberlain, Lift-Master, and Craftsman brand openers.” And it supports security features like automatic notifications when your door is left open, or every time it opens and closes.

Smart plugs are often a gateway to building out a smart home. And my favorite option, both for cost and convenience, is Tapo’s multipack of smart plugs.

Tapo sells its smart plug in a 2-pack at a great price—currently only $8 per plug. These plugs are compact and offer seamless, quick setup through the Home app without needing a separate app.

Controlling your thermostat entirely from your iPhone or a HomeView can prove extremely convenient. That convenience can also save you money by making it easier to stay on top of your electricity usage.

Aqara’s W200 smart thermostat is a beautifully designed, easy-to-use accessory that comes with a bonus Apple feature that’s hard to find: Adaptive Temperature, which can remove lots of the need to manually update the thermostat.

What are your top Apple Home accessory recommendations? Let us know in the comments.

#3350. TV’s Best Sci-Fi Thriller Is Officially the New King of Netflix

From's success is rare among TV shows. The MGM+ horror-thriller began in relative anonymity but has become one of the most-watched shows after four years. When it premiered in 2022 on Epix — just before the network rebranded to MGM+ — the platform was a niche, relatively unknown streamer that many viewers only encountered as a Prime Video add-on. Yet, fueled by relentless word-of-mouth and glowing endorsements from the likes of Stephen King, From steadily built a fiercely loyal cult following. Over four seasons, that organic audience growth transformed the series into the most-watched original show in MGM+ history.

Created by John Griffin, the series captures a specific vibe of mystery that is hard to replicate without collapsing on itself. While many mystery shows lose steam by piling on empty twists, From anchors its unknowns in a deepening lore that feels earned. Each season peels back another layer of the nightmarish town's curse, rewarding viewers without sacrificing its dread. Crucially, the mythology never overshadows the human element, thanks to excellent ensemble performances. Harold Perrineau delivers a career-best turn as Sheriff Boyd Stevens, alongside standout work from Catalina Sandino Moreno, Eion Bailey, David Alpay, and others.

The sleeper hit's trajectory then exploded into the mainstream when its first three seasons arrived on Netflix in October 2026. This exposed the show to an even bigger audience, and within weeks, the results started showing. From topped Nielsen's streaming charts with over five billion minutes viewed, proving the show's widespread appeal. As America celebrates Thanksgiving, From has received a massive boost on streaming and has surged to become the seventh most-watched show on the streamer in the US. Globally, it is the third most-watched show, behind the new horror hit The Body and the true-crime documentary The Trials of Karen Read. Meanwhile, From is preparing for one final season that ties everything together.

In April 2026, MGM+ confirmed that the hit horror-thriller had been renewed, but would end with Season 5. Principal photography kicked off in Halifax, Nova Scotia, in July 2026 and recently wrapped in late November, officially moving the final chapter into post-production. While MGM+ has yet to lock in an exact premiere date, the fifth season is slated to arrive in 2027. With the show's recent explosive success on Netflix, the final season is poised to be its biggest yet.

Watch the first three seasons of From on Netflix and the fourth on MGM+. Stay tuned to Collider for more updates.

#3349. 10 Hidden Controls Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

You can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely new side of the game.

If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

If you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

When you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

While driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

When you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

When buying a TV, knowing which TV panel type to buy can be the hardest part. I personally have an OLED right now, but before that, I had a super-budget 43-inch HD screen — not even 4K. And you know what? It did the trick.

If you're watching mostly Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video, HBO Max, Apple TV+, or the like, I think you'll be fine with a 4K or even HD panel. Of course, colors won't pop as much and the screen won't be as bright, but when you're on a budget, sometimes you have to sacrifice.

I know the TV world can be super overwhelming — trust me, I’ve been there. So let’s do a quick rundown of the differences between the three “premium” panel types.

So an OLED has lots of mini diodes inside the panel that emit light individually. This means there’s no backlight, unlike older TVs. This means OLEDs are better for higher contrast, better blacks, better color, and smooth motion for gaming.

QLEDs also use a light-emitting diode. Unlike OLED, a QLED panel has a backlight, which illuminates each diode individually. QLEDs are better for brighter rooms, as the panel itself tends to be brighter, but OLEDs can reach better contrast levels and color accuracy.

Mini-LED is something else entirely: it uses tiny LEDs (light-emitting diodes, like both QLED and OLED) — but thousands of them. That means each diode can pack a major color and brightness punch. Mini-LEDs can be brighter, blacker, and more colorful — all at once.

#3346. AI May Be Scanning Your Private Signal Chats

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

If you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads. Signal's end-to-end encryption keeps prying eyes out, but if you use agentic AI on your device, your chats may not be as locked down as you think.

Signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11. While Signal cannot guarantee that AI won't have access to your data, there are a few protections now available for those on iOS and Android as well.

The main workaround in Signal for now is to restrict screenshots and screen recordings inside the app, though this does not prevent AI agents from potentially grabbing content from other parts of your device. According to Signal's support documents, these protections will now be enabled by default on iOS 27 and Android with the latest versions of the Signal app.

#3345. Two Budget Smartwatches That Make Perfect Gifts

If you or someone on your shopping list wants a new smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from. The problem is, a lot of them can be quite pricey. Apple's cheapest smartwatch, the SE 3, starts at $249, and its other selections only skyrocket from there. On the flip side, the risk in picking a smartwatch that's too inexpensive is that the manufacturer likely made a series of sacrifices to get the price that low. At a certain point, the tradeoff just isn't worth it.

Luckily, you do have options. There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark. And while you shouldn't expect the same capabilities as you would on flagship wearables, these devices are perfectly usable, both as fitness trackers and smartwatches—all while spending well below $100 a pop. CNET put both smartwatches through their paces to make these determinations, so you know whichever model you get, you won't be picking up a wearable paperweight.

Contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter. Amazfit is its own company, and produces a wide selection of smartwatch options. The Bip 6 happens to be the company's latest budget smartwatch, with an MSRP of just $79.99. In most cases, a price that low would be a red flag for a smartwatch, but not in the Bip 6's case.

The Amazfit Bip 6 holds its own against other flagship smartwatches. That's true on a surface level: This watch looks your average smartwatch, rather than a cheap imitation. In fact, at first glance, I'd bet most people would assume the Bip 6 is actually an Apple Watch. It has a rounded square design with a large 1.97-inch display with a resolution of 390 by 450 pixels (though there's no Always-On display). This isn't a cheap display, either: Amazfit put an AMOLED screen on the watch, which looks great indoors—though CNET Labs struggled to see the screen in direct sunlight.

Where the Bip 6 really shines, however, is with fitness tracking. This watch supports GPS, which makes tracking outdoor runs possible without a smartphone. CNET Labs found that it takes about 10 seconds to find a GPS signal, but once it connects, you're set. While running, the Bip 6 reliably tracks your heart rate. CNET Labs compared its sensor to the Polar chest strap HR monitor and found it on par, though, like other smartwatches, the Bip 6 is slower at detecting heart rate spikes. You'll get data like cadence and stride while tracking runs, and strength training and muscle groups while working out indoors. For example, CNET Labs found that it correctly identified arm muscle exercises while testing the watch during a pilates session.

You also get some health and wellness features, too. The Bip 6 can measure heart rate variations, body temperature changes, sleep stages, and even your breathing quality. Its One Tap Measuring mode supports a single reading for heart rate, SpO2 (blood oxygen saturation), stress, and breathing rate, and it supports cycle tracking—though CNET specifies it can't track skin temperature like other smartwatches and health trackers. There's an optional subscription that provides AI coaching tools and looks out for health conditions like sleep apnea and insomnia. While health and wellness tracking is solid, note that CNET Labs found Amazfit's app, Zepp, to be confusing, since it simply displays your data without much context or explanation.

For an $80 smartwatch, the Bip 6 has an excellent battery life. CNET Labs found that the watch could be pushed to its limits—multiple workouts using GPS, heart rate tracking, keeping the display on during workouts—and still run for eight days before needing a charge. In fact, reviewer Vanessa Hand Orellana speculates you could push the Bip 6 to Amazfit's two-week battery life claim by limiting some of the most intensive settings and features. The only downside here is that there is no fast charging, so it will take about two hours to get back to 100%. But if you're only charging the watch once every week or two, that isn't much of a burden. There's also no charger in the box, so you'll need to use a separate USB-C cable.

As a smartwatch, the Bip 6 can be a mixed bag. CNET found that the UI was clunky and sluggish, and the OS requires some user intervention before it's as usable as a standard Apple Watch or Galaxy Watch. While the watch has a voice assistant, Flow, CNET found it to be borderline unusable. However, CNET says Android users can reply to texts with a keyboard or dictation without needing the assistant. iPhone users can't do the same by default, but by downloading a third-party app, they can jerry-rig the watch to send and receive texts.

Based on CNET Labs' testing, the Amazfit Bip 6 is one of the best budget smartwatches you can buy. For $80, you get a reliable workout tracker that looks like most standard watches on the market. And while you're making some sacrifices at this price point, they're largely worth it for $80.

While the Amazfit is a good choice for both iPhone and Android users, the Galaxy Fit 3 might be the best choice for Samsung users. This isn't an option for iPhone users, and while it works with all Android devices, you get some Samsung-specific perks if you have a Galaxy phone.

The Galaxy Fit 3 is even cheaper than the Amazfit Bip 6: This watch is only $60, which makes it among the cheapest smartwatches you can buy. Now, this doesn't look like your average smartwatch. Samsung opted for a fitness tracker-like design, with a long 1.6-inch (40mm) AMOLED display. But for a fitness tracker/smartwatch hybrid, it's a solid look.

In CNET's testing, one of the Galaxy Fit 3's biggest strengths is its battery life—though it pales in comparison to the Bip 6. When pushed to its limits, the Fit 3 can run three days in between charges, though Samsung claims you can get it up to 13 days with the right settings. While the Amazfit has it beat, the Fit 3 might sound like a dream compared to other smartwatches, even from Samsung. Unlike the Bip 6, the Fit 3 supports fast charging. You can fill the watch up completely in just over an hour.

CNET did find that the "smart" elements of this wearable were a bit lacking, however. The Fit 3 doesn't support voice dictation or mobile payments like other watches do, and unless you have a Galaxy phone, you won't be able to access the camera remote or sync your alarms. And while the Amazfit Bip 6's "Flow" is hardly reliable, the Fit 3 doesn't have an assistant at all. You can see incoming calls and decline (but not answer) them, and you can send prewritten responses to text messages, but not initiate them. Still, CNET found that Samsung added the essentials: You have an alarm, calculator, weather app, camera remote, and, of course, the Samsung Health app. (What kind of health tracker would this be without it?)

CNET found that the Fit 3 is a reliable fitness tracker, particularly for $60. You can track over 100 different workouts, and the watch automatically logs exercises like runs, walks, rowing, and elliptical sessions—if you enable auto-tracking, that is. It also supports swimming with its IP68 water resistance rating. CNET Labs found that the heart rate tracking was "generally accurate" when compared to the Polar chest strap, though its slower with registering heart rate spikes. Interestingly, the heart rate tracker was a bit delayed in testing, but once CNET reviewed the data in the health app, the data had corrected to be largely accurate. You also get high and low heart rate alerts, though no ECG app. (The $249 Apple Watch SE 3 also omits this feature.)

In CNET's testing, the sleep tracker on the Fit 3 was useful, if not entirely accurate. The watch can detect your sleep stages and look out for snoring using your Galaxy phone's mic. Like other health trackers, you get a sleep score, but CNET found it a bit inaccurate, since it rated a six and a half hour sleep session "Excellent" (91/100).

Still, the Fit 3 is really the only other smartwatch option at this price point that people should seriously consider. Until another company drops a product around this MSRP, you have two solid choices in the Amazfit Bip 6 and Galaxy Fit 3.

#3344. Veruschka One of the World's First Supermodels, Dead at 87

Veruschka, the German fashion icon widely regarded as one of the world's first supermodels, has died.

The legendary model -- whose real name was Vera von Lehndorff -- died Tuesday at her home in Berlin, surrounded by friends and family, according to German newspaper Bild.

Her sister, Catharina Kappelhoff-Wulff, confirmed her death in a statement on her fashion brand's website. A cause of death has not been disclosed.

Veruschka shot to international fame in the 1960s, gracing the cover of American Vogue 13 times and working with some of the biggest names in fashion photography, including Richard Avedon.

She also made her mark on the big screen ... appearing in the 1966 film "Blow-Up" and the 2006 James Bond flick "Casino Royale."

Long before supermodels became household names, Veruschka helped define what it meant to be one.

#3343. Three Reasons Not to Use ‘Buy Now, Pay Later’ During Black Friday

Gone are the days of needing to wait until after Thanksgiving to shop some seriously substantial Black Friday sales. As you're adding item after item to your cart during the sale, you might be tempted by offers for an "affordable monthly payment system." Also known as "buy now, pay later" (BNPL), the pitch is a tempting one: Buy what you need now, and pay later, "on your own timeline." But as convenient as it sounds, you should think twice before using buy now, pay later options, whether during Black Friday, Cyber Monday, or at any other time.

While BNPL plans can allow you to pay for purchases in installments without interest, they come with a cost that can easily outweigh any big discounts. Let's take a look at the hidden costs of BNPL, and why you're better off paying upfront for all your Black Friday purchases.

To be clear, Amazon doesn't have its own buy now, pay later program, and the company is not uniquely misleading on this front. The process is straightforward: you choose your items, select Affirm (a third-party lender) at checkout, complete a quick application, and receive an instant decision on your loan terms. Individual transactions initiated through Affirm are limited to $25,000, with a daily maximum of $100,000 across multiple purchases—but of course, your Black Friday splurge will be nowhere near that big, right? (Right?!)

The main draw of these programs is the ability to "pay at your own pace." If you are required to pay a down payment, that is due at the time of the transaction. From there, your first monthly payment is usually due one month after your purchase is processed. Each following payment will be due one month later, on the same day of the month.

You can choose your own timeline, usually spanning 3, 6, 12, or 24 months, depending on the purchase amount and your creditworthiness. Unlike traditional credit cards, Affirm shows you the exact payment amount and total cost upfront, and claims no hidden fees or compound interest.

You need a separate Affirm account in addition to your Amazon Prime membership. The application process requires basic information, including your name, mobile phone number, date of birth, and the last four digits of your Social Security number. Affirm performs a soft credit check initially, which doesn't impact your credit score, though they may conduct a hard inquiry for some loans.

BNPL plans are helpful if you really need to finance something big, but whenever possible, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses.

The ease of this sort of financing can make expensive purchases feel more affordable than they actually are. When you can buy a $1,000 tablet for "just $67 per month," it's easy to lose sight of the total cost, as well as your overall financial picture. In turn, this makes it all too easy to overspend on items you might not have purchased otherwise. You're better off taking a breath, stepping away from your shopping cart, and setting alerts to be notified when a product hits a price you can stomach, at a time you can afford it.

Despite what you may have heard in the past, BNPL providers may report to credit bureaus, meaning your BNPL purchases can in fact affect your credit score. For instance, all Affirm payments (including on-time, late, and missed payments) are now reported to the credit bureau Experian. So if you miss payments or default on the installment plan, it will cause damage to your credit score—making it even harder to get approved for mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and other financing down the road.

Still, not all BNPL providers report to credit bureaus or use the same type of credit check, so it’s important to understand the specific terms and practices of any service you’re considering.

When you use a credit card, you get valuable purchase protections like extended warranty coverage, price protection, and the ability to dispute fraudulent charges. BNPL plans generally don't come with these safeguards. This means you're on the hook if something goes wrong with your BNPL purchase and the retailer doesn't make things right. The smarter move is to only buy what you can afford during a sale, no matter how tempting those deals may seem.

Although installment plans are helpful if you really need to finance something major, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses. Better to wait for a good price for something you truly need and can afford to pay for right now.

If there's a big-ticket item on sale for Black Friday but it's still out of your budget, consider these two questions before you turn to BNPL through Affirm:

Is this really an essential purchase? BNPL should really only be used on completely necessary purchases that you can’t afford right now, but can afford in six weeks. On that note...

Will I be able to pay this off within six weeks? When a bigger payment gets broken down into smaller installments, you might find yourself overspending in the long run, because it "feels" like you can afford it. Stay on top of how much you’re actually spending—especially if you're considering multiple BNPL purchases—and how it will impact your overall budget going forward.

For more information about deals and discounts, keep an eye on all of Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

#3342. CBS’ ‘Matlock’ Officially Sets Season 3 Release Date

For the first time since its 2024 premiere, Matlock has not been on CBS's fall schedule, marking an intentional strategic shift rather than a cancellation. Series creator Jennie Snyder Urman requested the move to the network's midseason rollout after the central Wellbrexa investigation was resolved in the Season 2 finale. This extended nine-month break gives the writing team extra breathing room to craft a fresh mystery without compromising quality.

Production is already underway, with Kathy Bates returning as Madeline Matlock alongside Skye P. Marshall, who is also directing an episode this season. When Matlock Season 3 finally premieres on Thursday, January 21, 2027, it will also feature a slight schedule adjustment. The hit legal drama is moving from its previous 9:00 pm slot to 10:00 pm ET, airing directly after Elsbeth to anchor CBS's Thursday primetime lineup.

Matlock is one of several CBS shows with shorter seasons, with the network ordering just 13 episodes for Season 3, down from the usual 20-episode season. Fire Country and NCIS: Origins have also seen this change. As for where the story goes next, Urman confirmed it will remain in the healthcare industry and build on the Wellbrexa mystery, even though it won't be a direct continuation. The new arc involves insurance and healthcare. "We had a lot of pieces going in, so we really had to create this new piece of it. I feel lucky that the network’s giving us time to get it right because I don't want the quality to drop," she said, adding, "The quality is everything to me."

A great detective is really just a personality with a method attached, which is why we keep remaking the same four of them. Here is yours, what it says about you, and the case for them being the best in the business.

You let people think you are not a threat and then you simply never go away. Columbo is the only major detective show that tells you who did it in the first ten minutes, because the pleasure was never the puzzle, it was watching a rich man slowly realise he is in trouble.

You are the most interesting person in the room and you know exactly how to use it. Rian Johnson built Blanc as a gentleman detective who is also an outsider everywhere he goes, which lets him be charming at people who would never otherwise talk to him.

Everybody tells you everything, and you have never once asked them to. Jessica Fletcher is a crime novelist from a small town in Maine who is so warm and so obviously trustworthy that suspects confess to her essentially as a social courtesy.

You expect to be lied to and you are almost never disappointed. Chandler wrote Marlowe as a man with a rigid private code in a city that has none, which is why he takes the case, solves it, gets nothing out of it and takes the next one.

CBS has made some significant changes to its winter schedule as shows that had been delayed finally get slotted in. The new hit legal drama Cupertino is moving to Sundays at 10 pm beginning January 17, while the new comedy Eternally Yours is also moving to Mondays at 8:30 pm after a new episode of Ghosts. NCIS: Sydney takes over the NCIS: Origins slot beginning Tuesday, January 26, while Elsbeth moves to 9 pm and Matlock to 10 pm beginning Thursday, January 21. Ghosts airs the second all-new episode of the week at 8:30 pm after Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage to be able to fit its 22-episode sixth season into the schedule. Matthew Gray Gubler's new procedural Einstein airs on Fridays at 8 pm, while Sheriff Country moves to 9 pm beginning February 12.

Tune in to CBS on Thursday, January 21, to see what the new season of Matlock has in store. Stay tuned to Collider for more updates.

#3341. Skip the knockoffs: Real PITAKA aramid fiber cases start at $18.99 this Black Friday

Scroll through Amazon for five minutes and you’ll find dozens of $10–20 cases that look, through a thumbnail, almost identical to $50+ aramid fiber ones. Same dark weave, same slim profile, same pitch.

Once you actually snap one onto a phone, the differences are obvious. You handle your phone for hours every day, so rough seams around the charging port, awkward cutouts, low-quality materials will make you regret your purchase instantly. With PITAKA’s Black Friday sale taking up to 30% off selected cases, it’s worth breaking down what actually separates a real aramid case from a cheap lookalike, why you should spent the extra money on PITAKA’s high-quality cases.

Plenty of budget cases get the woven look by printing a pattern onto plain plastic. If you’re looking for that style, go for it, but it won’t behave like woven aramid fiber, which lets a case stay rigid and thin without adding much weight.

Even genuine aramid cases aren’t all made the same way. The weave, resin, thickness, and surface finish all change how a case feels in use. PITAKA uses woven aramid fiber in two main weights: 600D and 1500D. Those numbers measure yarn density; the finer 600D weave feels a bit smoother and produces a slightly thinner shell than 1500D. Whatever case you choose, look past the word “premium” and check whether the maker actually spells out what the case is made of.

Most aramid cases stick to plain black and gray. PITAKA’s Fusion Weaving method blends colored fibers and multiple weave styles directly into the shell instead of printing a graphic on the outside. PITAKA says the process requires tight control over fabric tension and how fibers cross between layers. In practice, it means you can pick something colorful like the Sunset colorway without giving up the feel of woven fiber, or stick with classic Black & Grey if you prefer a quieter look.

Online listings spend almost all their time showing off the back of a case, even though your fingers spend just as much time on the sides, buttons, and bottom edge. An awkward camera cutout makes quick shots annoying, a tight port opening fights bulkier charging cables, and sharp edges dig into your hand on a long call.

Rather than selling one shell in ten colors, PITAKA splits its lineup into three builds:

If you use a magnetic charger, wallet, or grip, how the magnets are built into the case matters just as much as the outer material. Sticking a separate magnet ring inside a shell usually adds extra layers and thickness.

PITAKA’s Amber Magnet Film process bonds coated magnets directly with the aramid fiber and resin under heat and pressure. That keeps the magnets enclosed without bulking up the case, which is the kind of detail you won’t spot in a photo but will notice in your pocket.

Spending more on a case doesn’t guarantee it’s better, and plenty of $20 cases are completely fine. Genuine aramid fiber by itself doesn’t guarantee better drop protection either. A thin shell like Edge is made for people who hate bulky cases. If drop protection is your main concern, look at a cushioned option like Cairn or Summa, and compare actual edge coverage and model-specific testing instead of judging by price or material alone.

What you’re really paying for with a higher-end aramid case is how it feels and fits every time you pick up your phone.

If you already want a thinner, better-finished case, Black Friday takes some of the sting out of the price. PITAKA’s Amazon offers run November 19–30, with discounts varying by device and colorway:

Buying directly from the PITAKA official website? Code PTKPR12 takes an extra 5% off from November 10 through December 31. It’s separate from the Amazon sale, so double-check eligible products and your final total at checkout.

NBA 2K27 only launched a few weeks ago, but the series is always good for a Black Friday saving.

That’s exactly what Amazon is offering, with the best-looking sports sim around reduced to under $30 for the Standard Edition on PS5. As you’d expect, it’s an evolution rather than a revolution year-on-year, but there are improvements to animations, female MyPLAYERs, and new MyCAREER Eras to explore.

It’s a basketball sandbox, and it’s better than half price.

Sony hasn’t launched a handheld since the ill-fated PlayStation Vita, but the PlayStation Portal might be the next best thing.

Capable of remote streaming while out and about, and streaming from your home console while you’re indoors, it’s an ideal way to play games like Grand Theft Auto 6 without taking up the whole telly (although, if you’re anything like me, your wife insists on watching it like it’s a crime drama TV show).

This deal nets you the Portal, as well as a handy accessories kit including a charging dock, carry case, outer shell, earbuds, and a screen protector at a $35 discount.

Another 2022 hit, Gran Turismo 7 saw Sony’s Polyphony Digital studio roar back with a racing sim that has some of the most stunningly detailed car models you’ll ever see - and it’s seeing a big discount at Target.

So good-looking that you’ll want to reach out and touch the steering wheel, the game is still getting updates to include new cars, tracks, and quality-of-life features.

Our reviewer awarded it 4.5 stars out of 5 in our review, and it’s only gotten better since then - particularly if you have a PS5 Pro.

It’s hard to believe it’s been nearly five years since it launched, but Elden Ring remains one of the best games ever made - and a must-play on PS5.

If you’ve picked up a console just for GTA 6 and missed out on this fantasy action-RPG, you can snag it for just $15 right now at Amazon.

It’s challenging, yes, but it’s also unforgettable. In fact, the PS5 version has a colossal 96-percent positive rating on Metacritic.

If you're a multi-platform gamer, this one is for you. The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni headset is currently $50 off at Amazon. The "Omni" in its name stands for two things: firstly it has an omni-directional mic for more natural vocal tones; secondly, it's compatible with PC, PS5 and Xbox. You can hook up to all three at once via USB for hi-res audio and simply switch between inputs as you need to. So handy.

As I noted in my SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni review, the sound quality is also excellent, the headset is super comfy and it features a zero downtime battery system with one battery charging in the USB hub as you use the other in the headset.

There's no shortage of games on sale today, including $10 off Assassin's Creed: Shadows at Amazon. "The best entry in the franchise since the good ol’ days of Ezio," is what our reviewer gave in her 4.5* Assassin's Creed: Shadows review. "Feudal Japan looks gorgeous and is brimming with activity and idle chatter, while the story itself is compelling... It’s even better than I’d hoped and I was fully invested after just a few hours of play."

The PlayStation Pulse Explore gaming earbuds have hit their lowest ever price for Black Friday, reduced from $199 to $119 at Amazon — a huge $80 saving. We gave these buds four stars in our PlayStation Pulse Explore review. We loved the immersive in-game sound and fantastic fidelity. There's multipoint connectivity so you can hook up to your phone, too.

If you often play at night and want to be able to fully enjoy the sound of your games without waking your family or neighbors, this is the deal for you.

Why not round out your setup with a shiny new TV? One of our favorite deals overall right now is on the TCL QM6K 75-inch 4K Mini-LED TV, which is currently over $300 off at Amazon. We gave this TV four stars in our review, and it's been a favorite of ours to recommend for a while now in the sub-$1,000 category. At just $697 with this deal, it's positively a steal.

Importantly, on top of its excellent picture quality, it features a 144Hz refresh rate, so you can max out that PS5 at 120fps. If you're playing GTA VI though, obviously, you'll only need 30 of those frames.

You can also follow our Black Friday TV deals coverage for more great TV deals.

When it comes to Star Wars games on PS5, most people will wax lyrical about Galactic Racer or Jedi Survivor, and don't get me wrong, both deserve their flowers, they're great games, but so is Star Wars Zero Company. Don't let it be forgotten!

Now on sale for $44 on Amazon, in this turn-based tactics game, you control the titular squad, a scrappy group of mercs and misfits, roped into a dangerous mission with high stakes. I'm not usually one for tactics games, but Zero Company really hooked me at launch because of its accessible combat design and its focus on player choice. If you play with "permadeath" switched on (and you should), squad members can die for good in battle, which means every decision you make feels important. There's a wealth of content and loads of ways to customize your team.

It's always useful to have an extra DualSense controller, either for co-op gaming or so you can switch between a couple to make sure you always have a fully charged pad.

Right now, PS5 DualSense controllers start at $54 on Amazon. This deal isn't just on the stock white model, but also on other color options like the slick Midnight Black. Or if you don't mind spending a little extra, for $64 you can get very funky designs such as the Rhythm Blue, Techno Red, or Remix Green.

So far, I've been sharing great deals on games I've already played (and enjoyed), but here's one I'm tempted to pick up for myself, on a title missed earlier this year.

Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is now $39 at Amazon. The prequel to the excellent Plague Tale games launched in August, during a crowded release period, so I didn't have time to play it over the summer. But I've heard great things, and as a fan of the Plague Tale series, this discount is just the nudge I need to circle back. Though I'll likely buy it and put it in my backlog, which is already overflowing.

Perhaps in an attempt to pry gamers away from Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest Call of Duty game, Modern Warfare 4, is on sale for $54 at Amazon — a $15 discount.

While very much the standard Call of Duty experience, that's not a bad thing, MW4 offers a rich suite of modes, with a single-player campaign, a new DMZ extraction mode, and the dependable range of competitive online modes. Shooting is zippy, as always with CoD, and new updates are rolling out at a constant clip, so there's always a new map to try or a new weapon or perk to unlock.

It doesn't reinvent the Call of Duty series by any stretch, but it serves up reliable FPS entertainment, and sometimes that's all you want out of a new online shooter.

The recently released Ghost of Yotei Complete Edition is $49 at Best Buy, a $20 saving on this package, which bundles the full GoY base game, the Echoes of Sekigahara single-player expansion, the Most Wanted survival mode, and the Legends online co-op mode. It's a whole lot of Ghost of Yotei at a reduced price.

It's not just the PS5 Pro suffering from stock issues this holiday season; the regular PS5 is also becoming very tough to find at MSRP. The likes of Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart are sold out, but at GameStop, you can get a PS5 Slim Digital Edition for $599 (aka its regular price). Meanwhile, if you're okay with a refurbished model, you can get a refurbished PS5 starting from $499 over on PlayStation Direct.

Saros is sort of like Sony's forgotten exclusive this year. Which is a real shame because, as I said in my Saros review, it's "a relentless, exciting and demanding rogue-lite shooter that combines cinematic spectacle with tight bullet-hell combat."

The spiritual sequel to 2021's Returnal, Saros is on sale for $39 (was $69), a great price for a thrilling bullet-hell shooter that deserved more attention at launch back in the spring. If you skipped it, then this deal is an excuse to fix that oversight.

During my time at Tom's Guide, I've reviewed dozens of PS5 games, The Last of Us Part II Remastered is one of only two I've given a full five-star score. Right now, you can pick up The Last of Us Part II Remastered for $27 (44% off) over on Amazon.

Did The Last of Us Part II need remastering? Maybe not. The original PS4 version still looks amazing to this day and plays perfectly on PS5, but if you've never experienced this modern masterpiece, this is the version to get. Aside from a few minor visual upgrades, you get new content like the addictive No Return mode, which puts a roguelike spin on TLOU 2's excellent combat. It's a PS5 game everybody should play!

If you demand value-for-money in your next PS5 purchase, the Kingdom Hearts Collection [I-III] for $59 (was $74) on Amazon is a deal you shouldn't ignore.

It offers the entire Kingdom Hearts saga to date (bar the Melody of Memory spin-off title released in 2020) in a single package. That's all 3 mainline games (and KH 3's DLC) and 7 interstitial titles (3 of which have been converted into HD movies). There's so much content here; you'll probably still be working through it all by the time Kingdom Hearts 4 launches in late 2027.

As a recent convert to the Kingdom Hearts series thanks to the very collection, I'm really enjoying my time so far, and this package makes for the ideal starting point.

If the wait until The Witcher 4 is getting you down, grab The Blood of Dawnwalker for $30 at Amazon (57% off its MSRP of $69). It's an RPG that wears its Witcher inspiration on its sleeve, probably because it was developed by ex-Witcher devs.

You play Coen, a young man on a quest to save his family from a ruthless vampire lord, who has become a Dawnwalker (essentially human by day, vampire at night). What makes this one special, aside from the strong quest writing and focus on player choice, is the day/night cycle. Completing quests or side activities moves the in-game clock forward, so you have to spend your time wisely. Waste it, and your family will meet a grisly fate. This mechanism adds real weight to every decision.

The DualSense Edge is the "pro" version of the stock PS5 DualSense controller, and for Black Friday it's on sale for $169 at Amazon, which is a solid $30 discount.

To justify its premium price, you get swappable stick modules, mappable back buttons, adjustable trigger lengths, and fully customizable button profiles. Plus, because it's a PlayStation product, it still includes adaptive triggers and haptic feedback — features that third-party pro controllers are forced to omit.

It has been cheaper during previous Black Friday sales (it's dropped to $149 in the past), but $169 is the lowest price I've spotted in 2026, so it's worth considering.

The mark of a good survival horror is if it sticks around in your psyche for weeks (even months) afterward, and that's definitely been the case with Silent Hill Townfall.

In my review, I called this "one of the most intense games I've ever played," and I stand by it. Set in a remote Scottish town and the first full Silent Hill game played in first-person, it's a nightmare experience, full of horrific sights and a bleak, dark atmosphere. It also looks stunning on PS5 and offers a cryptic but compelling story.

For Black Friday, Silent Hill Townfall is on sale for $29, down from its launch price of $49. That's a bargain price, particularly because with 5 unlockable endings, you'll probably want to play this game multiple times. Assuming you have the nerve for it.

Resident Evil Requiem is one of the best games released in 2026, and in my opinion, the best entry in the series when it comes to balancing horror and action. This is because of the dual protagonist setup, casting you as both fan-favorite Leon S. Kennedy and newcomer Grace Ashcroft. Leon's section is pure action, while Grace's really ramps up the fear. It's the best of both styles. It's also playable in both first and third person, or a mix of the two (which is the ideal way to play).

I'd recommend Resi 9 at full price, and did as much back in February when it launched. So, it's no surprise that I'm even more eager to encourage you to pick up now that it's more than 40% off ahead of Black Friday over on Amazon.

Hey all, I'm Rory, one of the biggest gamers on staff at Tom's Guide (and a 30+ year PlayStation fan), here to guide you through the next few hours of PS5 deal coverage.

Let's start with talking PS5 Pro. The souped-up PlayStation console has been in high demand this year, largely due to the launch of a certain GTA 6, so I've been tracking PS5 Pro restocks the last couple of months. While the console remains out of stock across major retailers even a week post-GTA 6's launch, I'm hoping that Black Friday itself could bring more stock. Surely, there will be restocks this side of the holidays?

I'll keep monitoring retailer listing, and report back if I catch sight of any stock, but if you want to check for yourself, below are all the retailer links you need right now.

Whether your original DualSense is at the end of its life or you want a second because you just bought a couch co-op game, you're in luck. The DualSense is discounted by $20 right now, so you can get one (or two... or three) for just $54 at Amazon.

Sony’s standard PS5 pad remains one of the best controllers around thanks to its responsive haptic feedback and adaptive triggers. Standard colorways, including White, Midnight Black, Cosmic Red, and Galactic Purple, are down to $54 at Amazon, beating PlayStation Direct’s sale price.

Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart is a stellar game for PS5 owners, and one that's so addicting that I didn't even realize it was 3AM when I was playing it. With its incredibly fun gameplay, satisfying balanced story, gorgeous graphics and music, and excellent use of PS5 features, you'll feel the same way.

Games, of course, don't always come cheap, and if you've been holding off on buying Rift Apart, time to hit "add to cart" now. It's discounted by 57% so you can get it for just $29 at Amazon right now.

So, this is one deal I've personally got my eye on because I'm thinking of getting it. Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is down to $54 at Amazon right now, and well-worth it for anyone who wants to live out their fighter pilot dreams.

The latest installment in the storied franchise boasts a full single-player campaign and the series' largest suite of online modes to date. With stunning visuals and sounds, it's the complete package — and this Black Friday deal doesn't break the bank either!

"Why do we fall, sir? So that we can learn to pick ourselves up. Batman begin," is what Michael Caine tweeted a couple years ago. He forgot the "s" at the end, and every time I think of the tweet, I laugh out loud. The tweet naturally went viral, and it even made its way into Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight.

That's enough reason to buy the game this Black Friday, which is down to $49 at Amazon.

Oh, you need more reasons? Fiiiiine. Lego Batman is extremely fun. It takes everything folks know about Batman from popular culture and filters it through the tried-and-true Lego formula. You'll love it.

I absolutely adore animals — sometimes I think I might like them more than humans, actually. If you're like me, you should play Planet Zoo, which is down to $32 at Amazon for Black Friday. I myself bought the game during last year's sale!

Those who played Zoo Tycoon back in the day will be familiar with how Planet Zoo works. In this wildlife park management sim, you build enclosures for your animals, look after them to ensure they're happy, and also keep up your guests' happiness and satisfaction levels. It's really, really fun.

Whether you've played the 1997 Final Fantasy VII or are a newcomer to the series, boy have I found some killer deals for you. Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade is a whopping 63% off right now so you can get it for $14, and its sequel, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth is also available for $14.

Remake Intergrade is a stunning game with excellent music, fun combat, a compelling storyline, and versatile playable characters. Rebirth is also a phenomenal JRPG thanks to its stellar graphics, robust customization options, and vast explorable environments.

Both games are must-play for PS5 owners, and the perfect way to pass the time until Final Fantasy VII Revelation comes out in 2027!

The DualSense is my favorite controller. Its haptic feedback and adaptive triggers deliver a truly immersive experience unlike any other. If you want to experience the full extent of the DualSense's capabilities, you need to play Astro Bot. Right now, it's down to $37 at Amazon.

"One of the best PlayStation games ever," is how we described it in our 4.5-star review of Astro Bot. This is a truly joyful platforming experiences that's elevated by its inventive level design and countless loving nods to PlayStation's rich history.

Trust me, this game will make you fall in love with the DualSense (if you aren't already).

Ghost of Yotei is one of the best PS5 exclusives of all time, and if you're a fan of Ghost of Tsushima, you need to play the sequel. In GoY, you play as Atsu, a female mercenary hunting down the Yōtei Six to avenge her family in 1603 Ezo.

In this highly cinematic single-player game, you embark on a visually beautiful journey with a compelling storyline. The massive open-world is stuffed full of activities, like petting foxes and defending wolf dens, and the music is just as gorgeous.

Right now, you can get the Complete Edition (including the Most Wanted DLC and Sekigahara story expansion) for just $49 at Amazon.

You can't play Mario Kart on the PS5 but Sonic Racing CrossWorlds is the next best thing — and it honestly makes MK look like child's play. It's one of the most memorable entries in the Sonic the Hedgehog series, and is a must-have for racing fans.

Packed with chaos, fun and presenting a bit of a learning curve, CrossWorlds wins big when it comes to smooth drifting and air tricks that give you significant boosts. Extensive kart and ‘Gadget Plate’ customization enable you to strategize in different ways and fine-tune your style.

If you fancy picking up a new racing game just in time for the holidays, Sonic Racing CrossWorlds is down to just $19 at Amazon — that's 50% off!

Fancy over-ear headphones instead? The Razer BlackShark V3 Pro is my current go-to headset — and one of the very few products I've awarded 5/5 stars to. I'd recommend these cans even at their full price, but you can grab them for just $199 at Amazon (their lowest ever price).

The BlackShark V3 Pro "makes me feel like I’m playing video games at the movie theater." That's how I described the sound quality in my review. These cans boast fantastic sound with spatial audio support that gives you a competitive edge. With highly effective ANC, you can truly feel like the main character.

Alongside controllers, I also test gaming headsets (I know, I have a very cool job). That includes headphones and earbuds designed specifically for the PlayStation. If you want a pair of earbuds that look uber cool and sound even better, I recommend the Sony PlayStation Pulse Explore.

When I reviewed them, I knocked a point off because of their high price — no more, though, as the earbuds are $80 off right now, so you can get them for just $119 at Amazon!

The Pulse Explore boast immersive in-game audio thanks to the planar magnetic drivers, while the fully customizable 3D audio profiles and multipoint connectivity truly elevate your gaming experience. They’re also extremely comfortable to wear during long gaming sessions.

I love Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order, but I love its sequel, Survivor, even more... and I wasn't expecting to see such a massive discount on it today! You can save $59 on Star Wars Jedi Survivor today as the game is down to just $10 at the PlayStation Store.

In Survivor, you play as Cal Kestis, accompanied by his trusted droid BD-1, as he continues his ongoing battle against the Galactic Empire and his quest to reunite the surviving Jedi. Thanks to satisfying lightsaber combat and fluid gameplay, as well as stunning graphics, Survivor is a must-play for Star Wars fans and casuals alike.

As you can probably tell by now, I'm an avid gamer. Thing is, my partner isn't. So I embarked on a simple mission: find couch co-op games that aren't overly complicated so that she can see how fun video games can be. That's when I found Unravel Two.

Unravel Two is a story-driven side-scrolling game where you and your partner play as a pair of adorable protagonists called Yarnies. A mix of chase sequences and platforming make it a wonderful game, and there's a compelling and beautiful storyline will be tugging on your heartstrings.

If, like me, you've got a loved one you really want to play games with, Unravel Two is the perfect starting point — and you can grab it for just $4 today!

5/5 star ratings are extremely rare at Tom's Guide, and 007 First Light is one of the only games we've awarded it to. It serves as the perfect origin story for James Bond, and it's the best 007 game since Golden Eye. As someone who'd fallen out of love with Bond, it made me care about the franchise again.

007 First Light's cinematic single-player campaign is "remarkable, offering a gripping, quintessentially Bond story, packaged together with some of the best action-adventure set pieces I’ve ever experienced." That's how our reviewer, Rory, described the game in his review. High praise!

This is a game you need to experience for yourself — and now you can, thanks to this Black Friday discount. 007 First Light is available for $34 at PlayStation right now.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is the 2026 remake of the 2013 hit game — and one that's loved by many fans. This Black Friday deal is too good to ignore, as it drops the game's price by 50%!

Black Flag Resynced is a wonderful remake. It looks gorgeous, adds worthwhile new content that adds to Edward Kenway's story, and makes loads of smart improvements. If you want to ignore the main story and do nothing but sail the stunning seas, go deep sea diving, be my guest. Being a ruthless pirate has never been this fun.

Assassin's Creed is one of my favorite franchises, and I've played every single entry in the series. Right now, many of them are down to their lowest ever prices across Amazon and the PlayStation Store. If you've been meaning to sink your teeth into one, now's the time.

For example, Assassin's Creed Origins (set in ancient Egypt) is down to just $8 at PlayStation — it usually costs $59!

I'm not a huge fan of horror games as I chicken out too quickly — but Alan Wake 2 is a game I keep coming back to. The Deluxe Edition (which includes the Night Springs and Lake House DLCs) is available for just $29 at Amazon right now.

Alan Wake 2 weaves together two compelling protagonists across a unique, multi-dimensional, narrative that is often seriously strange but still surprisingly engrossing. You solve various puzzles, take down different kinds of enemies with your flashlight and guns, and untangle the Dark Place's mystery.

Oh, and there's a fun musical number in there, too, and that alone makes the game worth playing!

Black Friday is the best time to pick up a new game, yes, but it's also the perfect time to pick up a new controller. As part of my job as a senior reviews writer, I test the best controllers for PC and consoles — and the Razer Raiju V3 Pro is one of my favorites for PS5.

The Raiju V3 Pro features TMR thumbsticks that offer precise control over movements while removing the risk of stick drift. Then you've got Hall Effect triggers that are highly responsive and customizable. The back buttons are removable, and personalization via the mobile app is quick and easy.

The only things you miss out with the Raiju V3 Pro are adaptive triggers and haptic feedback — which is the case with most third-party PS5 controllers. Small price to pay if you value precision over everything else, though, right? Right now, it's down to $156 from $219 at Amazon.

It's great that lots of AAA games are discounted for Black Friday, but if you want a cozy, easy-to-play game, I've got a fantastic recommendation for you. Neva is currently 50% off at the PlayStation Store right now, so you can get it for just $9.

Neva is a puzzle-platformer with barely any dialog, where the beautiful art design and stunning music do the talking for the game. It conveys a lovely story which you only understand when you reach the end, and it may drive you to tears — I sobbed like a baby.

Hello, one and all! Nikita here, taking over from Jason. I've just earned the Platinum trophy in Control Resonant so that's the first game I'm going to convince you to buy this Black Friday. Right now, it's down to $49 at Amazon — I'd even recommend buying it at full price so this is a steal!

As someone who loved the original Control, Resonant surpasses my expectations. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging; the soundtrack is immaculate; Dylan (the protagonist) is compelling as are the supporting characters; and the skill tree and various traversal abilities you can acquire are nothing like you've seen before.

Regardless of whether you're a fan of Remedy's games or not, this is a game you shouldn't skip. After spending over 60 hours with Resonant, it's my personal Game of the Year (GTA 6 who?).

I've played a lot of racing games this year, and out of all the arcade titles, I didn't expect Star Wars: Galactic Racer to be an absolute banger!

The premise is simple — a rogue-like kind of title where you blitz through different sets of races on different planets, randomized every time you go through with new upgrades as you go.

That's a nice tactical dimension added to what is some phenomenal racing gameplay. It takes me back to seeing Anakin in Episode One every time: the high-stakes competition rushing by at 400 MPH, the combat of it all. It is phenomenal.

Trust me, it's worthy of your $49 right now.

The audacity! I'm only in my mid-30s, but apparently one of my favorite games of 2026 is a "dad game"!? I feel like I just aged 10 years reading that sentence.

Oh...on a second read, turns out he's talking about how it's playing a Father-like figure in-game...I'll pass my apologies to Scott (may have got a little frustrated at him.

In that vein, he's absolutely right. It's a great little duo relationship between you two that connects on an emotional level — paired with unique sci-fi gameplay that is easy to get addicted to.

Read our Pragmata review, where we called it the surprise hit for 2026, and save $20 on it right now.

Silent Hill: Townfall is easily the best the series has been in 25 years. Screen Burn’s shift to first-person and a bleak, remote Scottish town breathes massive new life into the franchise, all while keeping its trademark atmosphere, visuals, and skin-crawling sound design completely intact. It’s properly horrific, genuinely unsettling, and I never wanted to stop playing.

Yes, just like the parody on GTA 6, this is indeed the remaster of the remake of The Last of Us. Chances are a lot of you have already played it!

But if you haven't (or you haven't played this version), the huge improvement in visual fidelity, animation and gameplay with more aggressive enemies and an increased focus on tactics, makes it well worth revisiting.

Also, well worth noting that this is without a doubt the best story ever told in gaming. There's a reason I have a tattoo dedicated to the game after all!

I mean GTA 6 is 212GB, and that's not even the worst of it (looking at you, Call of Duty). Today's games take up a lot of storage, and if you're reliant on the on-board space, you're going to fill that up fast.

That's why adding an SSD to your PS5 is becoming essential, and one of the best I've tested in terms of zippy speeds and strong sustained performance is actually one of the smallest.

The Sandisk Optimus GX 7100M can read/write just as fast as the onboard storage (GTA 6 loads within a few milliseconds of the time on SSD as it takes on the internal storage). And you can get $87 off it right now!

If your place is a little too cramped for a soundbar or surround sound speakers, a decent headset is the best way to really enhance the audio experience of Leonida as you play GTA 6.

And my personal favorites come from Nacon — the RIG R5 Spear for a wired option and the R8 Spectre Pro for a wireless afair.

The all-encompassing surround sound is seriously impressive (especially for the price you can get them now) with great attention to the finer details and nicely booming bass.

Right now, you can save big on both headsets, which gives you enough money leftover for these custom faceplates that give your cans a GTA flavor!

If you haven't tried this Miyazaki masterpiece that has won a whole bunch of game awards, you literally have no excuse now.

For the price of your average McDonald's meal, you can snag one of the best Soulslike games from the maker of Dark Souls — massive in scope, glorious in combat.

And at this price? It's one of those "don't even think about it" kind of deals to just snag right now.

So Wolverine is Insomniac's newest game, but its not their best. I'm torn between Ratchet & Clank and this masterpiece: Marvel's Spider-Man 2.

There's honestly nothing more satisfying gameplay wise than webbing your way across the city and fighting crime. Plus the storyline here is incredibly gripping and visually, it's stunning.

If you haven't got round to picking it up, it's 57% off right now. That is an absolute steal on this game!

So I bought Marvel's Wolverine at launch. Personally, I love it. It's no Spider-Man (more on that later as that is also discounted too), and at its full $69 price given the size and scope of it, I can appreciate that some folks may not be the biggest fans.

However, with $20 off? This is where it becomes a much more tantalizing prospect to become Logan and get super violent. It's a great story, looks incredible and the combat feels very satisfying.

So let me start with the bad news — the PS5 Pro is either out of stock or being scalped on the used market. If you see one of these for anything more than $1,000, do not buy.

Now to the good news for those who are keen to get in on the GTA 6 hype, but don't have the box to play it: there is PS5 stock available to grab! PlayStation's own certified refurbished program has some decently-priced systems, and GameStop has a brand new units too.

And yes, Walmart technically has the PS5 digital Slim too, but for $900!? Hell no.

Gran Turismo 7 plays great on a controller of course! But to really get the best out of it, you're going to need a racing wheel.

Yes, there is the Logitech G923 bundle for $120 off, but you'll be doing yourself a disservice with this one. It's a gear-driven wheel (using gears inside to identify steering movements and provide force feedback), which means it's not the most reliable and the feedback you get is week.

But that's where the Thrustmaster T598 comes in — arguably one of my favorite value racing wheels of the past few years. You get surprisingly strong direct drive and a great feel in a compact package.

And right now, it's also $120 off. The price is a little more than the Logitech, but it's so worth it for the night and day difference.

As you may already know about me, I'm the motor racing guy on the team — addicted to sim racing, and realizing just how different the real thing is.

One of the games that has stuck with me throughout my three decades of PlayStation gaming is Gran Turismo, and the 7th edition has had me hooked for hundreds of hours.

If you haven't played it yet, you owe it to yourself to get it for this dirt cheap price of $29!

Here I am getting my first PlayStation for my Birthday. Anyone can call themselves a "30-year PlayStation gamer," but dug this out for the special occasion that I get to take you through the best Black Friday PS5 deals!

I'll be sharing some of my favorite games on sale, accessories to really enhance your time playing and keeping a close eye on any console stock I find (as well as some personal tips).
