Khamosh Pathak is a freelance tech journalist with over 13 years of experience writing online. An accounting graduate, he turned his interest in writing and technology into a career. He holds a specialization in user experience design from ISDI Parsons in Mumbai, where he sought to deepen his understanding of UX, consumer devices, and interplay between software and technology.

Khamosh has written thousands of how-tos and guides on every major platform (iOS, macOS, Android, and Windows). He got started writing how-tos and guides for Guiding Tech, where he also published several e-books. His work has also been seen at MakeUseOf, How-To Geek, and PCMag. He is truly passionate about brewing good coffee.

Google loves a rebrand. What started off as "Spark" is now "Task" in Gemini—not to be confused with Google Tasks, the to-do app. Google took its Spark AI agent, which used to live in a separate tab, and integrated it into the Gemini interface. Gemini Task is available globally, and it’s completely free to use for some. That said, some features are limited to the U.S. and, of course, subject to some pretty strict usage limits. While not exactly a replacement for ChatGPT Dots or Meta Muse, you can think of Gemini Task as a controlled version of an AI agent that can do quite a lot in the background.

To use Task, open Gemini and create a new chat. You’ll see a Task tab next to Chat. Switch to it, and start writing your prompt. (You’ll also see some suggested options here.) Type your task or action and press "Send." The feature works best if you’ve already enabled Personal Intelligence on your Google account, and have connected services like Gmail, Google Drive, and Photos as well. You can then tag “@Gmail” to use your Gmail account, or even a third-party connector. Task natively supports automation, so you can say something like, "run this task once every day," and the AI will add it to your Scheduled Tasks section.

Of course, I did the thing that every AI demo wants you to do: I asked Gemini to create a daily morning briefing for me, highlighting all important emails, calendar appointments, and tasks. And, in my experience, it works really well. It reminded me of this article's due date, that I have a couple of pitches in my inbox to review, that a credit card bill is due soon, and that there are some holidays around the corner.

Gemini is very good at retrieving information from emails and taking action. For example, I created an automation that collects all my coffee orders for the month and presents the data in Google Sheets. I then asked Task to create a subscription manager for me. Instead of paying for a third-party app, it took a few minutes to collate the services I pay for into one list. It even accounted for the currency differences (some subscriptions are in USD, some in INR) and gave me a tally in INR, along with things like average monthly cost, and more.

While Gemini can connect to the open web, it's quite a hostile place right now for an AI bot. Websites are blocking agents from accessing their pages, which hinders their effectiveness. I asked Gemini to create a task that monitors the price of the Sony WH-1000XM5 headphones daily. For this, it asked my permission to spin up a remote browser, and loaded up Amazon, only to be blocked instantly. It did succeed in opening Croma though (a national retailer in India), but it took almost a minute for it to figure out that the price had not dropped below what I asked for. Would it be quicker and less resource-intensive if I did this myself? Yes, but the fact that Gemini can do this every evening like clockwork is the real advantage—as long as the websites comply, that is.

If you're going to try Task in Gemini for free, there are some limitations you should know about. The free plan only lets you run tasks once per day, and you can’t be granular about the exact timing. (Paid Gemini plans have no such restrictions.) You can only run 10 tasks at the same time, while the limit is 50 tasks for AI Pro users. Compute-based usage limits will also apply, based on your plan. The free access is currently live in India, the U.S., Canada, Australia, Japan, and South Korea.

Some features, though, are only for U.S. users. Gemini’s feature that lets you call businesses on your behalf is restricted to the States, as is the ability to forward emails to [email protected] to automatically turn the contents of the email into a task (like adding a college schedule to your calendar). U.S. users can also connect their Google Wallet account to set up payments at supported stores.

Gemini Task is not a proactive agent, nor is it trying to be. You still have to check the work. You have to approve any important steps, and if a website blocks AI models, there’s not a lot Gemini can do about it. For someone like me, who’s all-in on the Google ecosystem, I do see value in Gemini Task. The deep and robust Gmail integration is worth it alone. If you’re on the free plan, set up a couple of background tasks related to Gmail, Google Drive, or background research that run every morning, and call it a day. And if you’re paying for AI Pro, you can get a lot more done.

There comes a point on Thanksgiving when the kids are getting restless, dinner is still an hour away and everyone has run out of things to talk about. Believe it or not, ChatGPT might be the most entertaining guest at your Thanksgiving gathering.

While you've probably heard that the chatbot can help you plan your menu, figure out how long to cook a turkey and come up with creative ways to use leftovers, some of my favorite ways to use ChatGPT have absolutely nothing to do with cooking.

From hosting a family game show to creating an interactive holiday mystery or even building a playable video game in seconds, ChatGPT can bring the whole family together in some surprisingly creative ways.

So, before everyone retreats to their phones or falls asleep on the couch, here are five ChatGPT prompts to keep the whole family entertained this Thanksgiving.

When you're done with the board games, you can turn ChatGPT into a game show host. All you need is to use Voice Mode to have the chatbot read questions aloud, keep track of scores and announce the winner.

The fun part is that you can tailor the questions to the people in the room. Mix Thanksgiving trivia with pop culture, general knowledge and funny facts about your family.

Try this prompt: Act as an energetic game show host for our Thanksgiving gathering. Create five rounds of questions that appeal to both kids and adults, including Thanksgiving trivia, pop culture, riddles and silly challenges. Ask one question at a time, let us answer and keep track of each team's score. Include a dramatic final round.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

If you've already taken the obligatory Thanksgiving family photo, upload it to ChatGPT and have a little fun with it.

Ask ChatGPT to reimagine everyone as characters in an '80s sitcom, passengers aboard the Mayflower or royalty attending an extravagant medieval feast. You could even turn your family into the stars of a fictional Thanksgiving movie.

Let everyone take turns choosing a theme and vote on the funniest result. You might end up with something worth framing.

Try this prompt: Transform this family photo into a hilariously dramatic 1980s sitcom promotional poster for a fictional Thanksgiving special. Give everyone period-appropriate outfits, exaggerated expressions and big hairstyles while preserving their recognizable facial features. Come up with a funny title for the show.

Who stole Grandma's pumpkin pie? Why has the turkey mysteriously disappeared? And why is Uncle Bob suddenly refusing to answer questions?

ChatGPT can create an interactive mystery game in which everyone at the table becomes a detective. Unlike a traditional mystery game, the chatbot can respond to your questions and introduce new clues as you play.

You can customize the difficulty depending on who's participating and keep the mystery lighthearted if younger children want to join in.

Try this prompt: Create an interactive, family-friendly Thanksgiving mystery called "The Case of the Missing Pumpkin Pie." Introduce five suspicious fictional characters, each with a motive and a secret. Let us investigate by questioning suspects and examining evidence. Keep the culprit a secret until we make our final accusation. Make the mystery solvable in about 15 minutes.

One of the most entertaining things you can do with ChatGPT is build your own simple browser-based game without knowing how to code.

And Thanksgiving lends itself to some wonderfully ridiculous ideas. Imagine a game in which a turkey has to escape the dinner table, a pumpkin pie falls from the sky or a player has to dodge flying Brussels sprouts.

Have everyone contribute an idea, then ask ChatGPT to combine them into a playable game. Depending on your ChatGPT interface, you may be able to preview it directly or save the generated HTML file and open it in a web browser.

Try this prompt: Build a playable browser game called "The Great Thanksgiving Escape." The player controls a turkey trying to escape a kitchen while dodging flying vegetables and collecting pumpkin pies for bonus points. Include colorful retro arcade graphics, keyboard and touchscreen controls, a high score and a restart button. Make everything work in a single HTML file with no external dependencies.

This might be my favorite idea because it could lead to conversations you wouldn't otherwise have around the dinner table.

Ask ChatGPT to host a personalized version of a "Most Likely To" game or a family edition of The Newlywed Game. Everyone writes down their answers before revealing them, and the person with the most matching answers wins.

The questions can be funny, nostalgic or completely unexpected. Just keep them away from anything that might reignite an old family argument. ChatGPT can help entertain your relatives, but there's only so much it can do about Thanksgiving drama.

Try this prompt: Host a funny, heartwarming game of "How Well Do You Know Your Family?" for our Thanksgiving gathering. Give us 20 questions, one at a time, that encourage us to guess each other's answers. Include childhood memories, favorite foods, funny habits and ridiculous hypothetical situations. Keep everything lighthearted and appropriate for all ages.

So much of the conversation around AI focuses on how it can help us get more done and be more productive. But one of the things I enjoy most about ChatGPT is experimenting with what it can do when there's absolutely nothing I need to accomplish.

This Thanksgiving, rather than disappearing into your phone while everyone else scrolls through theirs, try using ChatGPT to get everyone laughing, talking or playing something together. Who knows, you might just start a new Thanksgiving tradition.

#3305. New Gemini setting lets you keep chat history, but turn off AI training [U]

Update 11/24: This new setting is now widely rolling out. On gemini.google.com, tap the settings gear icon to find a new “Gemini History” item at the very bottom. This opens myactivity.google.com/product/gemini with an On/Off dropdown.

Under “Help train generative AI models with,” you’ll find the new “Chat content including text & attachments” setting. It’s enabled by default.

Your future chats won’t be used to train generative AI models, unless you provide feedback.

Training on “Audio and Gemini Live videos & screenshares” remains an opt-in preference.

Original 11/16: Gemini’s existing Keep Activity setting “controls how long your chats are saved and whether they are used to train generative AI models.”

Google is now separating that preference into two new options.

This is huge. One of the major things Siri-AI users on iPhone like to point out is that while their assistant is a less capable portmanteau of Siri and Gemini, their queries are not used for AI training. Gemini on Android, on the other hand, offers the superior AI platform with the caveat that there is no way to opt out of training and still retain your chat history. Until now. Now users of Gemini on Android get the best of both worlds - the best of Google's AI models powering their AI experiences and their chat history siloed from AI training.

The first setting is called “History” and lets you “control how long your history is saved.” If disabled:

“…future chats will be saved for around 2 months and used to respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public, with help from human reviewers.”

The duration is currently 24 hours for chat context, and 72 hours to help protect Google, users, and the public.

The second setting allows you to “separately control whether your chat content, including text and attachments, is used to train generative AI models.”

With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training.

If Keep Activity is currently off, the two “new settings will both be off.” These changes are rolling out over the “coming weeks,” and Google is notifying users via email.

There comes a point when your child is old enough to potentially get their own Kindle, mostly so they stop stealing yours and filling up your library with Big Nate collections.

Now is the perfect time to find the right Kindle for your child, as Amazon typically puts many of its Kindles on sale for Black Friday. You may not have known that Amazon has kid versions of the Kindle, Paperwhite and Colorsoft.

Unfortunately, none of them are on sale, and in general they're more expensive than their "adult" counterparts. But Amazon also offers a bit more out of the box with the kid versions.

Let's break down what you get with the Kid Kindle and why the higher price may be worth it.

To be up front, as far as we can tell, the different Kindle Kids eReaders are the same hardware that you get with the standard Kindle, Paperwhite and Colorsoft.

The difference is that the Kid version comes with a case included. Right now, the Paperwhite Kids can be purchased with the Pirate theme, "Bookman," or Lakeside Retreat.

Additionally, the Kid Kindles come with a 1-year Kids+ subscription included. Basically, this is a more curated version of Kindle Plus (the rebranded of Kindle Unlimited) for children. It includes thousands of books for kids ages 6 through 12, like the Percy Jackson series or Diary of a Wimpy Kid. Also, the Kid version does not come with ads or distractions.

The Kid Kindles also have parent controls that can be accessed through the Parent Dashboard mobile app which can be used to suggest books or set screen limits.

Amazon updated most of its Kindle lineup earlier this year, but the 2024 version of the Kindle Paperwhite Kids is still available and the only Kids eReader on sale at $149. This version comes with 16GB of storage, a case, 6 months of Amazon Kids+, and a waterproof design.

By comparison, the adult Kindles do not come with a case, only three months of Kindle+ (which adds a cost), and you have to choose ad-supported or without lockscreen ads (again more expensive).

There are content controls and parent controls on normal Kindles, but in my experience, it's more finicky and usually requires a separate account if you truly want to lock things down. Quite annoying when you're sharing with your child and your wife is filling the library with romantasy novels. Not yet, buddy, not yet.

Both the kids and adult versions can be used to access library books through the Libby app, literally the best thing about Kindles compared to most other eReaders.

Here's the big difference: price. Let's use the Kindle Paperwhite as our example.

The Ad-free, 3-month Kindle+, Paperwhite costs $219 when its not on sale. The ad-supported version costs $199. The new Kids Kindle Paperwhite costs $229.

For a less expensive option, the cheapest standard Kindle is $149, while the Kids version costs $179. The case adds up the Kids version, but if you want a case for the adult version, the cheapest one I saw on Amazon tacks on $21 to the price.

If money isn't as big of a concern, the Kids Kindle Colorsoft is $299 but is great for kids who starting to read comic books or if you want the option for color stories. The base adult Colorsoft starts at $289 but there is a bundle with a case for $301, which is on sale.

Amazon refreshed the Kids Kindle this year with a thinner and lighter version. It features a 6-inch glare-free display, a themed case, and 1-year of Kids+ subscription. The Kids Kindle has up to 6 weeks of battery life and you can listen to audio books using Bluetooth headphones. Parents can control settings with the Parent dashboard.

The big difference is that I rarely see the Kid versions go on sale while the standard Kindles get discounted throughout the year typically around Black Friday, the new Spring sale and the big Prime Day summer sale.

Also, the subscription. You get three months of Kindle+ which normally costs $11.99 per month (or $143.88) for a year. The Kid Kindle comes with 12 months of Kids+, which normally costs $7.99 a month for Prime Members or $8.99 if you don't have an account.

Additionally, if you have other Amazon devices like the Amazon Kids Echo or an Amazon Kids tablet, your Kids+ subscription is accessible across each device with a child profile.

The upfront costs of the Kid Kindle is higher in general, but over the first year, if you keep the subscription, you're paying on par with the adult Kindle and getting more control and curation.

As we noted above, you don't have to get the newest model and Amazon has done a decent job of supporting much older Kindles.

In this case, don't let the sticker shock get to you and consider the Kindle Kid, Kindle Paperwhite Kid, or Kindle Colorsoft Kid for your child.

#3299. Now Is the Best Time to Buy a New Ring Camera, With Prices at 60% Off for Black Friday

If you’re browsing home security options, Ring has one of the best Black Friday deals that should be on your radar. Right now, you can add an indoor camera and another one at your front door for less than $65. The Ring Indoor Cam 2K is 58% off at $24.99 (originally $59.99), while the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is 60% off at $39.99 (originally $99.99)—both at their lowest-ever price.

Both offer features like 2K video and two-way talk, but the indoor cam is the simpler purchase if you mainly want to check on a pet or kids and see what’s happening near an entrance. It plugs into an outlet, so there’s no battery to recharge, and its low-light color video helps preserve detail when lights are off or dimmed. However, since it’s a fixed-view camera, keep in mind that you’ll need to position it carefully.

The Battery Doorbell is the better pick if alerting you to visitors, deliveries, and potential intruders is your priority. It has a 140-degree horizontal and vertical field of view that provides head-to-toe framing, plus up to 6x zoom for better detail. You can install it without wiring, though you’ll need to recharge its built-in battery. It also requires a 2.4GHz wifi network.

The main catch with both devices is the ongoing subscription cost: Live viewing, two-way talk, and basic real-time notifications all work without a subscription, but reviewing saved footage requires a paid plan, starting at $4.99 per month or $49.99 annually for one device; coverage for multiple devices at one location starts at $9.99 monthly or $99.99 annually.

At these prices, the Ring Indoor Cam 2K is perfect for occasional live check-ins, while the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is better suited to monitoring your front entrance. Buying both makes sense if you already have a Ring plan that covers extra devices.

#3295. Thanksgiving Earthquake Hits Off Baja California Coast, Magnitude 5.7

A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck a remote group of islands off Mexico's Baja California peninsula on Thanksgiving ... delivering a holiday shake-up in the Pacific Ocean.

The quake hit Thursday near the Revillagigedo Islands, roughly 216 miles from Cabo San Lucas, at a depth of about 6 miles.

Fortunately, the remote location means the earthquake is unlikely to affect many people ... though it's unclear whether any aftershocks could strike closer to the mainland ... and the region was already rattled by a magnitude 4.2 earthquake just one day earlier.

The Revillagigedo Islands are volcanic and federally protected by Mexico, boasting such a rich marine ecosystem that National Geographic has dubbed them the "Galápagos of Mexico."

The Thanksgiving tremor comes just days after back-to-back earthquakes shook Southern California's beach cities ... including a magnitude 3.2 quake in Orange County early Monday and a magnitude 3.3 quake off Manhattan Beach on Sunday.

Mexico also experienced a magnitude 4.7 earthquake in Baja California earlier this month.

For now, it appears the holiday got off to a shaky start, with no major destruction.

More about convenience than chasing top speeds, you can use the Roam 7 as a standard router, connect it to public wifi to create a private network, or share your phone's internet through USB tethering. It also supports Ethernet input and USB modems, along with range extender and wireless client modes. That flexibility is particularly useful when you’re juggling a laptop, phone, and maybe a tablet and would prefer not to sign each one into a shaky network separately. Setup is straightforward through the TP-Link Tether app: scan a QR code, choose your connection type, and you’re online in a few minutes.

Once it’s running, the hardware covers the basics, with a 2.5 Gbps port for a wired connection like a hotel’s Ethernet jack, a 1 Gbps port for a wired device, and a USB 3.0 port for a storage drive or phone tethering. And since it draws power over USB-C (5V/3A), a basic power bank can keep it going through a long layover or a camping trip. As handy as it is on the road, though, it’s not meant to replace a full-size home router—even with its 5 GHz band and Wi-Fi 7 support—which will generally offer better coverage and more consistent speeds. Real-world performance also depends heavily on your connection and setup. USB tethering, for example, can feel slower than using your phone directly. It also leaves out features like automatic band steering, so you may end up managing networks yourself. Still, if you travel often or need a portable network hub for multiple devices, you’ll find it holds up pretty well.

#3292. Dolly Parton Honored by U2 During Emotional NFL Thanksgiving Eve Halftime Show

Dolly Parton's voice echoed through SoFi Stadium Wednesday night ... as U2 paid tribute to the late country icon during a moving Thanksgiving Eve halftime performance.

The rock band took the stage during the Los Angeles Rams' matchup against the Green Bay Packers ... with frontman Bono singing alongside Dolly's prerecorded vocals on their duet "Torn," as images of the country legend appeared on curtains surrounding the stage.

The tribute was especially emotional because "Torn" is believed to be Dolly's final recorded song before her death in August at age 80, following a private battle with cancer.

Dolly recorded her vocals in June, just two months before she died ... and Bono later told Rolling Stone she actually got out of bed while battling her illness to record the track.

As TMZ previously reported ... Dolly's final recorded song is about a family torn apart by conflict, with lyrics touching on broken relationships and the pain of loved ones turning against each other. Bono has described the track as Dolly's final prayer for America.

U2 also treated fans to classics including "Sunday Bloody Sunday," "Where the Streets Have No Name," and "Pride (In the Name of Love)" during the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game.

#3291. Apple Mail added four convenient new features in iOS 27

iOS 27 brought new features to Apple Wallet, Maps, Notes, Messages, and more—and it includes key upgrades for the Mail app too. Here’s everything new for Apple Mail in iOS 27.

If you have much history using Apple Mail, you’ll know that its search feature hasn’t always been the best. But in iOS 27, search has gotten a big upgrade.

More relevant search in Mail. A new ranking system brings the most relevant results to the top to help you find what you need right away — even if it’s buried deep in your inbox.

I can’t count the number of times search has previously failed to find messages that I knew existed. So far in my usage, iOS 27 has fixed that.

Suggestions at the top of messages have been in Apple Mail for years. But in iOS 27, they have a new, more flexible design and expand to support third-party apps.

When Mail detects that you might want to take action on the contents of an email, a suggestion might appear at the top of the message. These include: directions in Maps, creating events in Calendar, tracking a shipment with Apple Wallet, and more.

In iOS 27, third-party apps can offer suggestions too. And when multiple apps are available with suggested actions, there’s a drop-down menu to show you all available options.

Smart Reply is a keyboard feature that automatically surfaces reply options you can utilize with a single tap.

In iOS 27, the next generation of Apple Intelligence comes with improvements to Smart Reply.

Apple says that Smart Reply “can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.” Essentially, rather than offering fairly generic reply options, now Smart Reply suggestions will actually sound a lot more like you.

Apple has added ‘Ask Siri’ buttons throughout Apple Mail, just like the rest of its system apps. And Siri AI brings a bunch of new powers for Mail users.

One example I’ve seen several times on social media is that you can ask Siri to delete all messages from a specific sender that’s spamming you.

While tech can get pretty expensive, especially in our current "RAMageddon" era, there are still plenty of affordable devices out there. If you're looking for a portable Bluetooth speaker, for instance, you don't want to buy something with poor sound quality, or that doesn't easily connect to your devices, or that breaks unexpectedly.

JBL's Go 4 is a small speaker, but it gets surprisingly loud—especially for a speaker at this price point. Like other JBL speakers, it places a particular emphasis on bass. This is a tiny speaker, so don't expect a subwoofer on the go, but not only will it let you hear the bass in your music, it is noticeably punchy. JBL advertises seven hours of playtime on a single charge here, which is often plenty for taking the speaker out and about for the day. Khloé Kardashian has been single for years ... but she's apparently open to walking down the aisle again, even if her future husband isn't into women.

The reality star revealed she's down for a "lavender marriage" during Thursday's episode of "The Kardashians" ... after influencer Colt Paulsen suggested the unconventional arrangement while chatting with her at a perfume launch party.

For those unfamiliar, a lavender marriage is typically a marriage of convenience between a man and a woman, where one or both partners are queer.

Khloé didn't immediately shoot down the idea ... telling Colt she'd be open to it, though she admitted in a confessional that taking care of another person isn't exactly high on her wish list.

But she does have one requirement for a potential gay husband ... joking that if he can make her look pretty every day, she's sold.

The admission comes after Khloé recently revealed she's been celibate for five years and identified as demisexual ... meaning she needs an emotional connection before developing sexual attraction.

As for her dating history ... Khloé hasn't been romantically involved with anyone since her messy split from Tristan Thompson, with whom she shares two children, True and Tatum.

She's previously said she's intentionally staying single to focus on her kids ... but apparently, a husband who doubles as a glam squad might just change her mind.

I write a lot about e-readers and e-ink tablets for Lifehacker, and one issue I'm constantly grappling with is how to write informatively about a bunch of devices that can be quite different in some details, like build or native firmware, and pretty much identical in others, given that literally all e-ink devices use display technology produced by the same Chinese company. If you are a shopping for a mattress for back pain in the Black Friday sales, there's a few things to keep in mind. 1. Choose a mattress with lumbar support Your lumbar region is the curve at your lower back. A mattress with enhanced lumbar support will support this natural ‘S’ shape, comfortably filling this gap and distributing your weight evenly. The Saatva RX, Saatva Classic and Helix Midnight Luxe are just a handful of mattresses that support the lumbar beautifully. 2. Opt for the right firmness It’s a common misconception that when it comes to back pain, the firmer the mattress the better. Instead, most chiropractors recommend a medium-firm mattress as the sweet spot between pressure relief and support. However, those who weigh over 230lb or are back or stomach sleepers might find relief from a firmer mattress. Check out our guide on how to choose a mattress for more advice on mattress firmness.

Should you buy a mattress from Amazon this Black Friday?

You can buy anything at Amazon, even a new mattress — but should you? I'm going to have a quick scout around to see if any new deals have dropped at Amazon overnight. In the meantime, check out my pros and cons of buying a new mattress from the online marketplace below.

✅Cheap deals: You can often pay less for a mattress on Amazon than if you were to buy it directly from the brand, even if it is only on certain sizes.

✅Faster shipping: The Black Friday sales can cause an increase in demand, leading to shipping delays and back orders. Amazon, on the other hand, is known for their speedy delivery — a huge plus if you need a bed before Christmas.

✅More options: Brands run out of stock or discontinue certain models when revamping their collections. Amazon gives you the chance to buy discontinued models and items that are sold out on the brand’s website.

❌No guaranteed sleep trials or warranties: The beauty of buying directly from a brand is that their benefits are clearly outlined, such as a sleep trial. While Amazon usually offers 90-100 day returns, they don’t offer official trials which allow you to sleep on your purchase for an allotted number of weeks to see if it's right for you.

❌Less reputable: While you can find mattresses and bed toppers from trusted brands at Amazon, there are a lot of cheaper beds from less well known brands that you may be tempted by, but aren’t always the best quality.

Why can you trust us to guide you towards the right mattress for you? Collectively, our team has clocked up over 24,000 hours testing mattresses. We approach mattress testing from two distinct viewpoints; what does it feel like to sleep on night after night? And how does it perform during our objective tests? In addition to sleeping on it for a minimum of three weeks, during which time we invite friends and family members to offer their feedback, we conduct a series of tests in sleep studio lab. Here, we test against motion isolation, temperature control and pressure relief. You can find out more about how we test mattresses in our mattress methodology.

There's quite a bit of variety here, too, from battery-powered projectors you can take camping or move between rooms to more powerful 4K models designed for a dedicated movie-night setup.

The Soundcore Nebula P1i is down to $299 from $399, while the Nebula P1 is $699.99, down from $799. Both offer 1080p resolution and Google TV, but their speaker setups are what make them interesting. The P1i has two 10W speakers that flip out and rotate to direct sound toward your seating area, while the P1's speakers detach completely and can run wirelessly for up to 20 hours. The P1 is also brighter at 650 ANSI lumens versus the P1i's 380, though you'll need a power outlet for either projector since neither has a built-in battery.

Small enough to slip into a bag, the Nebula Capsule 3 and Capsule 3 Laser are worth considering if you want something you can easily take on trips or move around the house. Both offer 1080p resolution, automatic image adjustments, and up to 2.5 hours of battery life, although the Laser model is a little brighter at 300 ANSI lumens compared with the standard model's 200.

Taking movie night outdoors is a little easier with a battery-powered projector, and both the Nebula Mars 3 Air and Mars 3 are designed for just that. The smaller Mars 3 Air is down to $519.99 from $599.99, offering 1080p resolution, 400 ANSI lumens of brightness, and up to 2.5 hours of playback. The larger Mars 3, now $899.99 from $999.99, steps things up with 1,000 ANSI lumens, up to five hours of battery life in Eco mode, and a more powerful 40W speaker. If you're ready to move beyond 1080p, the Nebula Cosmos 4K SE at $1,099.99 (originally $1,299.99) offers a more affordable way to get 4K resolution. Its hybrid LED and laser light source delivers up to 1,800 ANSI lumens, while its Dolby Vision support helps bring out more detail in compatible movies and shows. You also get Google TV and automatic image adjustments for easier setup, though it doesn't have a built-in battery, so you'll need a power outlet nearby.

At the premium end of Nebula's lineup, the X1 and newer X1S are designed for a more serious home theater setup. The X1 is down to $2,299 from $2,999, saving you $700, while the X1S is $2,799 from $3,299. Both use triple-laser technology with 4K resolution, Dolby Vision, and optical zoom, but the X1S has a considerable advantage in brightness, reaching up to 6,000 ANSI lumens compared with the X1's 3,500. #3283. Atomically Thin Materials Significantly Shrink Qubits

MIT researchers use 2D materials for capacitors in quantum circuits in an effort to scale processors

Superconducting quantum processor and its microwave packaging.

Quantum computing is a devilishly complex technology, with many technical hurdles impacting its development. Of these challenges two critical issues stand out: miniaturization and qubit quality.

IBM has adopted the superconducting qubit road map of reaching a 1,121-qubit processor by 2023, leading to the expectation that 1,000 qubits with today’s qubit form factor is feasible. However, current approaches will require very large chips (50 millimeters on a side, or larger) at the scale of small wafers, or the use of chiplets on multichip modules. While this approach will work, the aim is to attain a better path toward scalability.

Now researchers at MIT have been able to both reduce the size of the qubits and done so in a way that reduces the interference that occurs between neighboring qubits. The MIT researchers have increased the number of superconducting qubits that can be added onto a device by a factor of 100.

“We are addressing both qubit miniaturization and quality,” said William Oliver, the director for the Center for Quantum Engineering at MIT. “Unlike conventional transistor scaling, where only the number really matters, for qubits, large numbers are not sufficient, they must also be high-performance. Sacrificing performance for qubit number is not a useful trade in quantum computing. They must go hand in hand.”

The key to this big increase in qubit density and reduction of interference comes down to the use of two-dimensional materials, in particular the 2D insulator hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The MIT researchers demonstrated that a few atomic monolayers of hBN can be stacked to form the insulator in the capacitors of a superconducting qubit.

Just like other capacitors, the capacitors in these superconducting circuits take the form of a sandwich in which an insulator material is sandwiched between two metal plates. The big difference for these capacitors is that the superconducting circuits can operate only at extremely low temperatures—less than 0.02 degrees above absolute zero (-273.15 °C).

Superconducting qubits are measured at temperatures as low as 20 millikelvin in a dilution refrigerator.Nathan Fiske/MIT

In that environment, insulating materials that are available for the job, such as PE-CVD silicon oxide or silicon nitride, have quite a few defects that are too lossy for quantum computing applications. To get around these material shortcomings, most superconducting circuits use what are called coplanar capacitors. In these capacitors, the plates are positioned laterally to one another, rather than on top of one another.

As a result, the intrinsic silicon substrate below the plates and to a smaller degree the vacuum above the plates serve as the capacitor dielectric. Intrinsic silicon is chemically pure and therefore has few defects, and the large size dilutes the electric field at the plate interfaces, all of which leads to a low-loss capacitor. The lateral size of each plate in this open-face design ends up being quite large (typically 100 by 100 micrometers) in order to achieve the required capacitance.

In an effort to move away from the large lateral configuration, the MIT researchers embarked on a search for an insulator that has very few defects and is compatible with superconducting capacitor plates.

“We chose to study hBN because it is the most widely used insulator in 2D material research due to its cleanliness and chemical inertness,” said colead author Joel Wang, a research scientist in the Engineering Quantum Systems group of the MIT Research Laboratory for Electronics.

On either side of the hBN, the MIT researchers used the 2D superconducting material, niobium diselenide. One of the trickiest aspects of fabricating the capacitors was working with the niobium diselenide, which oxidizes in seconds when exposed to air, according to Wang. This necessitates that the assembly of the capacitor occur in a glove box filled with argon gas.

While this would seemingly complicate the scaling up of the production of these capacitors, Wang doesn’t regard this as a limiting factor.

“What determines the quality factor of the capacitor are the two interfaces between the two materials,” said Wang. “Once the sandwich is made, the two interfaces are “sealed” and we don’t see any noticeable degradation over time when exposed to the atmosphere.”

This lack of degradation is because around 90 percent of the electric field is contained within the sandwich structure, so the oxidation of the outer surface of the niobium diselenide does not play a significant role anymore. This ultimately makes the capacitor footprint much smaller, and it accounts for the reduction in cross talk between the neighboring qubits.

“The main challenge for scaling up the fabrication will be the wafer-scale growth of hBN and 2D superconductors like [niobium diselenide], and how one can do wafer-scale stacking of these films,” added Wang.

Wang believes that this research has shown 2D hBN to be a good insulator candidate for superconducting qubits. He says that the groundwork the MIT team has done will serve as a road map for using other hybrid 2D materials to build superconducting circuits.

Dexter Johnson is a contributing editor at IEEE Spectrum, with a focus on nanotechnology.

#3282. The Latest Apple Watch Is Up to $100 Off for Black Friday

Apple's latest flagship smartwatch, the Apple Watch Series 12, is worth the upgrade. With this model, Apple has upgraded the processor, added a new heart rate sensor, and improved the display durability. It's certainly one of Apple's best smartwatches, but that also means it isn't cheap: All these new features give the new Series 12 a starting price of $399, which only increases if you choose a model with cellular data. However, for Black Friday, you can take up to $100 off the Series 12, bringing the starting price down to $299.

The three biggest hardware upgrades with the Apple Watch Series 12 are the heart rate sensor, the S11 chip, and Ceramic Shield 2. That heart rate sensor now checks your pulse every five seconds, or 20 times a minute. Apple says the Series 12 checks your heart rate variability 24 times more than the Series 11, and your background heart rate 60 times more frequently than the Series 11. The company is even so bold as to say the Series 12 has the most accurate heart rate monitor on a wearable.

Powering the new heart rate monitor is the S11 chip, Apple's latest processor for the Apple Watch. The S11 isn't only responsible for these new heart rate features, however. In addition to running the same watchOS 27 features as other compatible Apple Watches, the S11 on the Series 12 can run Audio Intelligence, Apple's new suite of AI-powered audio features. That includes "Live Rewind," which lets you see a transcript of the last 15 seconds of an in-person conversation, and "Siri Recaps," which displays summaries of your conversations throughout the day. Finally, the other major advantage with the Series 12 is Ceramic Shield 2. This is a display upgrade that Apple typically reserves for more premium Apple Watch finishes, but this year, the aluminum Series 12 gets it as well. That means the watch should be more durable against scratches and cracks, without you having to upgrade to the more expensive model.

How much you'll save on a Series 12 depends on the size, color, and model. At this time, Amazon is selling certain colors of the 42mm Series 12 for $299, while certain colors of the 46mm option run $449 (also marked down by $100). You can also save on the cellular models as well: The 42mm option is currently $429 (down from $499), while the 46mm model is $449 (down from $549).

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

#3281. If You Loved 'The Good Daughter,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. In 2018, Jeff published the book Writing Without Rules: How to Write & Sell a Novel Without Guidelines, Experts, or (Occasionally) Pants. He holds a bachelor’s degree in English and previously worked in medical publishing as a production editor.

When not writing, Jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

There are plenty of reasons Peacock’s The Good Daughter is so damn watchable. The performances, for one—Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy are terrific as estranged sisters Sam and Charlotte Quinn. But it’s also a great story, tracing the corrosive effect of a years-ago trauma on the women and their lawyer father (Brendan Gleeson) amid the slow revelation of many extremely dark secrets. If you want more of that flavor of trauma-driven drama with a tight focus on family bonds, there’s one movie you should watch: 2015's Dark Places.

You want buried secrets? Dark Places has seriously buried secrets. Adapted from the Gillian Flynn novel, the film follows Libby Day (Charlize Theron), who survived the mass murder of her family in 1985. The crime is blamed on her brother Ben, a moody loner whose conviction was based in large part on Libby’s own testimony. For a long time, Libby is financially sustained by donations from people who sympathize with her plight, but three decades after the murders, the money has dried up, and Libby is desperate—so desperate, she agrees to help out a “true crime” club that believes her brother is innocent and is working toward his release.

Like The Good Daughter, Dark Places is anchored by a sibling relationship reshaped by the impact of horrifying violence. Libby and Ben’s experience mirrors Sam and Charlie’s in many ways, including in the way both Libby and Ben carry secrets for years after the terrible events that took family from them. The stories are also both compelling mysteries, slowly revealing the shocking truths behind one horrific night, and ultimately allowing the characters to better understand one another.

Dark Places also explores the insular, suffocating nature of small-town life, and how rumor and gossip become a poisonous presence in people’s lives. Libby, Ben, Sam, and Charlie all have to deal with others' assumptions and revelations that they've been betrayed by those closest to them, leading to powerful resolutions. If you loved The Good Daughter, you’ll love this movie. Stream Dark Places on The Roku Channel or Kanopy, or rent it on Prime Video.

Want more stories about family dynamics around secrets, violence, and explosive emotional confrontations? Here are a few more movies fans of The Good Daughter are bound to enjoy.

There’s no violent crime at the heart of this slow-burn drama—just an explosive chaos agent named Kym, played by Anne Hathaway. If your favorite aspect of The Good Daughter was the relationship between sisters Sam and Charlie, then this movie is perfect. Released from rehab to attend her sister’s wedding, Kym is self-hating, angry, and haunted by a terrible event from her childhood. Her sister, Rachel (Rosemary DeWitt), is welcoming, but has never truly forgiven Kym, and the simmering tension between the sisters and the rest of the family drives a drama that you won’t be able to look away from. Stream Rachel Getting Married on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

If you really vibed on the Southern setting, the slow-burn mystery, and the exploration of flawed justice in the modern age depicted in The Good Daughter, check out Where the Crawdads Sing. It’s a slower, dreamier rumination on rural life, violence and its cost, and small-town justice, but it hits the same sweet spot in its story about a woman named Kya (Daisy Edgar-Jones) who was raised in an isolated house in the swamps of North Carolina. Accused in 1969 of a murder, Kya’s story stretches back to her childhood, when she’s slowly abandoned by her entire family, leaving her at age seven to survive on her own. Ostracized as the “swamp girl” by the town, Kya fights to live her life and be loved while facing the unwanted—and violently persistent—attention of the murder victim. It’s about broken families, deeply buried secrets, and what we do to survive. Stream Where the Crawdads Sing on Hulu or rent it on Prime Video.

The Good Daughter is about life in a small, Southern town, family trauma, and the legal system—which makes A Time to Kill the perfect movie to watch when you finish the show. When a Black man’s daughter is sexually assaulted in Mississippi and her attackers—local members of the Ku Klux Klan—look likely to go free, he violently and publicly murders them. Local lawyer Jake Brigance (Matthew McConaughey) takes on the case, assisted by law student Ellen Roark (Sandra Bullock). They face violent opposition, withering racism, and an unfair legal system that echoes the environment in The Good Daughter in ways fans will appreciate. Stream A Time to Kill on YoutTube or rent it on Prime Video.

The Dry might be as close as you can get to The Good Daughter in terms of tone and story. Although set in Australia instead of the American South, The Dry is a story driven by past crimes and buried secrets in a rural setting just like the show. Twenty years ago, Federal agent Aaron Falk (Eric Bana) fled his hometown when he was suspected of the murder of his girlfriend. When his childhood friend, Luke, appears to have murdered his wife and young son before killing himself, he returns to investigate. The slow revelation of two mysteries—one in the past and one simmering in the drought-stricken present—makes this an ideal companion film to the show. Stream The Dry on The Roku Channel, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Set in Boston instead of the South, and focused on male friendships instead of a sisters’ bond, Mystic River nevertheless nails the same atmosphere of dread as The Good Daughter. In 1975, boyhood friends Jimmy, Dave, and Sean are traumatized when Dave is abducted and assaulted by two men. In 1990, the three men remain connected in their Boston neighborhood—Jimmy (Sean Penn) is an ex-convict still connected to local crime, Sean (Kevin Bacon) is a State Police detective, and Dave (Tim Robbins) is a blue-collar worker still haunted by his experience. When Jimmy’s daughter is found murdered and Dave seems implicated, Sean and Jimmy launch investigations from either side of the law, with Dave’s fate hanging in the balance. The ending is powerfully brutal, but this story of secrets and suspicion will resonate with fans of the show. Rent Mystic River on Prime Video.

#3279. PrismML’s Bonsai 2.5 brings better coding and tool use to on-device AI

Back in July, PrismML claimed its roughly 4 GB, 1-bit Bonsai 27B was the first AI model of its size to run on an iPhone. Now PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an update to the model it introduced in September.

The startup also drew attention when CEO Babak Hassibi told CNBC that Apple was evaluating its technology, as we reported at the time.

The new model is based on Qwen3.8 27B and keeps the same 5.9 GB footprint in its most compact format. This time, PrismML focused on helping the model handle longer tasks, including figuring out what to do when a tool returns an unexpected result or a step fails.

Bonsai 2.5 improved on six of the seven benchmarks PrismML highlights. Its SWE-bench Verified coding score rose from 60.8 to 75.6, while its AppWorld tool-use score jumped from 51.2 to 90.5. LiveCodeBench v6 dipped from 83.8 to 83.0.

What could that look like on a Mac? A coding assistant could inspect a private project, make a change, run the tests, and use the results to revise its fix. A document app could summarize a folder of sensitive files while keeping the processing on the device.

PrismML says Bonsai 2.5 runs on Mac, iPhone, and iPad through MLX. Its Apple silicon package is about 8.9 GB, and the model card walks through setup on a Mac. The weights are available for free under Apache 2.0.

For a closer look at how the model was compressed and tested, read PrismML’s technical white paper.

#3277. I Tried Coros' New 'Expedition-Focused' Smartwatch, and I'm Impressed

Coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” update to the Vertix 2 and 2S. Coros says it pairs the brand's brightest display yet with long battery life, and after unboxing it myself, I can definitely say it has a more refined feel that could indeed suit the office as well as the summit.

This watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight. The Vertix 4 will be available to buy starting on Black Friday, Nov. 27, but it won't exactly be at a discount: It costs $799, a $100 increase over the Vertix 2S.

That price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still. For instance, the Suunto Vertical 2 steel model costs $599, and the Garmin Fenix 8 is currently on sale for $749.99 at Amazon.

I've only just started testing the Vertix 4 and haven't even had enough time to get through its substantial battery life, but I can share some first impressions, particularly in how it compares with the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro that launched earlier this year.

Built-in flashlights have become a must-have feature on premium sports watches, and now the Vertix 4 is the first Coros watch to get one. Coros has departed from the usual layout, though. Garmin, Suunto and Amazfit put the light on top of the watch, but Coros places it on the side, between the digital dial and the back button.

Previous Vertix watches used a memory-in-pixel (MIP) display. MIP has advantages, most notably longer battery life, but I know I much prefer the vibrant display on AMOLED screens, like on the Vertix 4. It is the biggest visual change and a large part of why the watch looks more premium than its predecessors.

Coros claims up to 30 days in watch mode, or 10 days with the screen always on. It also quotes 48 hours of multi-band GPS tracking with the screen always on. I haven't had time to test these claims properly, so stay tuned.

Coros watches are high-quality sports watches, but don't expect to find all the little lifestyle features you've come to expect on a more traditional smartwatch:

Music: It can store tracks, but only files you drag and drop onto the watch. It doesn't pair with streaming services.

Payments: There is no NFC payment support.

Watch faces: Customization is more limited than on rivals.

On paper, the Vertix 4 looks like a significant upgrade: a better display, a more attractive design, a flashlight and satellite maps, at a price well below the Fenix 9 line-up. The $100 increase and cheaper alternatives like the Suunto Vertical 2 and discounted Fenix 8 will matter to some buyers, as will the limited smart features.

#3276. How AI Will Change Chip Design

Artificial intelligence’s promise and potential for the semiconductor industry

Rina Diane Caballar is a contributing editor covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment.

An array of semiconductor wafers are ready to be made into chips.

The end of Moore’s Law is looming. Engineers and designers can do only so much to miniaturize transistors and pack as many of them as possible into chips. So they’re turning to other approaches to chip design, incorporating technologies like AI into the process.

Samsung, for instance, is adding AI to its memory chips to enable processing in memory, thereby saving energy and speeding up machine learning. Speaking of speed, Google’s TPU V4 AI chip has doubled its processing power compared with that of its previous version.

But AI holds still more promise and potential for the semiconductor industry. To better understand how AI is set to revolutionize chip design, we spoke with Heather Gorr, senior product manager for MathWorks’ MATLAB platform.

How is AI currently being used to design the next generation of chips?

Heather Gorr: AI is such an important technology because it’s involved in most parts of the cycle, including the design and manufacturing process. There’s a lot of important applications here, even in the general process engineering where we want to optimize things. I think defect detection is a big one at all phases of the process, especially in manufacturing. But even thinking ahead in the design process, [AI now plays a significant role] when you’re designing the light and the sensors and all the different components. There’s a lot of anomaly detection and fault mitigation that you really want to consider.

Then, thinking about the logistical modeling that you see in any industry, there is always planned downtime that you want to mitigate; but you also end up having unplanned downtime. So, looking back at that historical data of when you’ve had those moments where maybe it took a bit longer than expected to manufacture something, you can take a look at all of that data and use AI to try to identify the proximate cause or to see something that might jump out even in the processing and design phases. We think of AI oftentimes as a predictive tool, or as a robot doing something, but a lot of times you get a lot of insight from the data through AI.

What are the benefits of using AI for chip design?

Gorr: Historically, we’ve seen a lot of physics-based modeling, which is a very intensive process. We want to do a reduced order model, where instead of solving such a computationally expensive and extensive model, we can do something a little cheaper. You could create a surrogate model, so to speak, of that physics-based model, use the data, and then do your parameter sweeps, your optimizations, your Monte Carlo simulations using the surrogate model. That takes a lot less time computationally than solving the physics-based equations directly. So, we’re seeing that benefit in many ways, including the efficiency and economy that are the results of iterating quickly on the experiments and the simulations that will really help in the design.

So it’s like having a digital twin in a sense?

Gorr: Exactly. That’s pretty much what people are doing, where you have the physical system model and the experimental data. Then, in conjunction, you have this other model that you could tweak and tune and try different parameters and experiments that let sweep through all of those different situations and come up with a better design in the end.

So, it’s going to be more efficient and, as you said, cheaper?

Gorr: Yeah, definitely. Especially in the experimentation and design phases, where you’re trying different things. That’s obviously going to yield dramatic cost savings if you’re actually manufacturing and producing [the chips]. You want to simulate, test, experiment as much as possible without making something using the actual process engineering.

We’ve talked about the benefits. How about the drawbacks?

Gorr: The [AI-based experimental models] tend to not be as accurate as physics-based models. Of course, that’s why you do many simulations and parameter sweeps. But that’s also the benefit of having that digital twin, where you can keep that in mind—it’s not going to be as accurate as that precise model that we’ve developed over the years.

Both chip design and manufacturing are system intensive; you have to consider every little part. And that can be really challenging. It’s a case where you might have models to predict something and different parts of it, but you still need to bring it all together.

One of the other things to think about too is that you need the data to build the models. You have to incorporate data from all sorts of different sensors and different sorts of teams, and so that heightens the challenge.

How can engineers use AI to better prepare and extract insights from hardware or sensor data?

Gorr: We always think about using AI to predict something or do some robot task, but you can use AI to come up with patterns and pick out things you might not have noticed before on your own. People will use AI when they have high-frequency data coming from many different sensors, and a lot of times it’s useful to explore the frequency domain and things like data synchronization or resampling. Those can be really challenging if you’re not sure where to start.

One of the things I would say is, use the tools that are available. There’s a vast community of people working on these things, and you can find lots of examples [of applications and techniques] on GitHub or MATLAB Central, where people have shared nice examples, even little apps they’ve created. I think many of us are buried in data and just not sure what to do with it, so definitely take advantage of what’s already out there in the community. You can explore and see what makes sense to you, and bring in that balance of domain knowledge and the insight you get from the tools and AI.

What should engineers and designers consider when using AI for chip design?

Gorr: Think through what problems you’re trying to solve or what insights you might hope to find, and try to be clear about that. Consider all of the different components, and document and test each of those different parts. Consider all of the people involved, and explain and hand off in a way that is sensible for the whole team.

How do you think AI will affect chip designers’ jobs?

Gorr: It’s going to free up a lot of human capital for more advanced tasks. We can use AI to reduce waste, to optimize the materials, to optimize the design, but then you still have that human involved whenever it comes to decision-making. I think it’s a great example of people and technology working hand in hand. It’s also an industry where all people involved—even on the manufacturing floor—need to have some level of understanding of what’s happening, so this is a great industry for advancing AI because of how we test things and how we think about them before we put them on the chip.

How do you envision the future of AI and chip design?

Gorr: It’s very much dependent on that human element—involving people in the process and having that interpretable model. We can do many things with the mathematical minutiae of modeling, but it comes down to how people are using it, how everybody in the process is understanding and applying it. Communication and involvement of people of all skill levels in the process are going to be really important. We’re going to see less of those superprecise predictions and more transparency of information, sharing, and that digital twin—not only using AI but also using our human knowledge and all of the work that many people have done over the years.

Rina Diane Caballar is a writer covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment. An IEEE Spectrum contributing editor, she's a former software engineer based in New Zealand.

#3275. Football Practice and Red Dirt Music: On the Field With Oklahoma Band Keyland

There is arguably no better day for football — watching it or playing it — than the autumnal crispness of Thanksgiving. But on this particular late summer afternoon, despite triple-digit temperatures and the Oklahoma sun making it feel even hotter, football is the sweat-drenched task at hand: Coach Kyle Ross is putting me through practice. It’s not lost on either of us that Ross’s primary job is coaching high-energy junior-high athletes in the state’s flagship football program, at Bixby, and I’m an out-of-shape journalist in his late 40s. If I finish Ross’s drills upright and healthy, we’ll declare it a success.

“What are you? Three-for-three or four-for-four catching passes here?” Ross — who is also the founder and frontman of the band Keyland — asks me. My football career ended in high school, 30 years ago, but I was a slot receiver with a reputation for catching anything thrown my way. What would my parents say if I started dropping passes now? “I will throw my body on this turf to not miss a pass,” I promise him.

Over the next few months, Ross will attempt to strike a rather unique balance as coach and touring artist. He’ll headline and sell out the Mercury Lounge in Tulsa, 30 minutes north of Bixby, open an East Coast run for Morgan Wade, and announce a series of 2027 dates supporting Kaitlin Butts. And while he’s ostensibly promoting Knuckle Sandwich, Keyland’s third studio album, Ross will always have football season in the back of his mind.

“I haven’t found anything better to do,” Ross says of why he continues to coach. “Except for maybe, get paid to play guitar and drink beer.”

Few pastimes are as all-encompassing in Oklahoma as football. Its two largest college programs — Oklahoma and Oklahoma State — play their home games in modern stadiums to sold-out crowds on most Saturdays in the fall, but it’s the high-school version of the sport that unites the state. Students, fans, and parents fill stadiums in the state’s urban cores and rural farm towns every Friday night, and for the past decade, no program has dominated this landscape like Bixby’s. The varsity Spartans are eight-time defending champions in Oklahoma’s largest class and this season were ranked No. 1 again by the state’s largest media outlet. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

This is Ross’s program. He’s an assistant coach for Bixby’s eighth-grade team and a junior-high English teacher. He grew up in rural Missouri, playing football through high school. Shortly after graduating college, Ross befriended Tyler Schneider — Bixby’s longtime offensive coordinator. The two hit it off, and within weeks, Ross joined the Spartan’s staff. Seven years later, Ross is throwing passes to me on the same turf that those Spartans play their home games. We’re here to talk about music, but I am here to experience what it’s like being one of Ross’s players.

“Let’s go!” he shouts as I haul in another pass. “And he scores!”

As it happens, that particular end zone is where I scored my last touchdown as a player. Before Bixby became the state’s juggernaut program, it was a mid-sized school in the same conference as my hometown team, the Okmulgee Bulldogs.

When he’s playing as Keyland — Ross uses the moniker interchangeably for his solo and full-band shows, named for a duck club he and his father used to hunt near his Chillicothe, Missouri, hometown — he wears an infectious smile that’s integral to his show. He describes the irreverent Knuckle Sandwich, which Keyland recorded at the Sonic Ranch studio outside of El Paso, as a product of pals hanging around for several days and finding music at the end of it. Related Content Jason Scott and the High Heat Are the Cool, If Raunchy, Band Americana Music Needs Honky-Tonk Woman: Kaitlin Butts Is As Ambitious As She Wants to Be You’ve Been Streaming ‘Broken Window Serenade.’ This Is the Texas Band Who Wrote It Wade Bowen Is Texas Music

“This album is about taking what you do seriously, but not taking yourself seriously,” Ross says. “That kind of embodies the whole creative process in recording it. It’s more of a hang than anything, and we get music at the end of it.”

It’s a microcosm for his entire music career. He had a guitar growing up, but played it sparingly. It was not until he was in college and caught a Chris Stapleton gig that he decided to give music a try. “I fell in love with Chris Stapleton, and that was the entry way to the long rabbit hole I fell into,” he says.

Landing a full-time job right in the heart of Tulsa’s music community was a bout of good fortune. Ross befriended Brandon Clark, frontman of the Red Dirt outfit BC & the Big Rig and highly respected in Red Dirt circles. Clark has a weekly gig at Mercury Lounge, and in 2022, he suggested that Keyland get booked at the bar.

Keyland’s first Mercury Lounge show was opening for the Big Rig. Shortly afterward, venue general manager Ashley Kirkley booked Keyland as a headliner. The show sold out, and Keyland have been a regular since.

“Keyland is a great band, no doubt, but the energy and charisma that emanates from Kyle is palpable at every show,” Kirkley says. “Beyond being an incredible performer with a distinctive voice that is unlike anything I’ve heard, he is also one of the most down to earth, kindest people I have ever met. Kyle is always striving for greatness in everything he does. He’s an incredible human, and we are incredibly lucky to have him as a part of our music family.”

Keyland have since gone on to, at least, regional notoriety. Ross has been booked multiple times at nearby Cain’s Ballroom, playing alongside the likes of Johnny Mullenax and opening a sold-out show for Josh Abbott earlier this year.

“Everyone’s at different levels of what they’re doing,” Ross says of the Tulsa music community. “I have friends who have sold out a place like Cain’s. I’m friends with people who are doing house shows for ten people. It almost seems like everyone has a very similar mindset of, ‘We’re almost there.’”

Ross knows better than anyone that Keyland is growing at a fast clip. He is likely to come to a crossroads between coaching and making music before too many more gigs or summer practices pass. But until then, he’s happy to pull double duty. And even at Bixby, where the focus is annually on another state championship, he has found support. He had a fan from the start in Schneider, but he’s brought most of the Spartans’ coaching staff onto his bandwagon — and even a few players.

“There’s a huge Venn diagram of coaches’ interests outside of football, and one of them is music,” Ross says. “All the coaches are super supportive. We have over 20 coaches, and a huge number of them have been to more than one concert. It’s just a community-oriented place to work. The kids, as they get older, they start to appreciate it.”

And on that note, practice is over. Ross’s actual players are starting to trickle in to Bixby’s behemoth of a training facility. Ross gives me a Bixby Spartans shirt for surviving his drills. “Didn’t die. No passes dropped,” he deadpans.

#3274. These Are the Best Black Friday 2026 Deals on Kindles and E-Readers

Score the year's biggest savings during the Black Friday sale on the best e-reader deals as they launch in real time. Follow our Black Friday Live Blog for live coverage of the absolute best deals, flash sales, and tech savings. For a deep dive into top-rated offers, expert buying guides, and exclusive discounts, explore our Best Black Friday Amazon Tech Deals page.

Amazon's Black Friday sale is in full swing, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save big on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the company introduced a new model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

If you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

If you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is currently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

If you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

If you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, currently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.)

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (currently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

For about $30 more than the X4 Classic, you can upgrade to the Xteink X4 Pro, which happens to be Lifehacker's e-reader Gift of the Year pick. It offers all the perks of the other Xteink devices, with two critical quality-of-life upgrades: A touchscreen for easier navigation, and a temperature-adjustable front light so you can read it in a dark room. (Less obviously, it also has a slightly faster processor that makes the whole thing feel a little snappier.) Right now, the X4 Pro is at its lowest price ever when ordered directly from Xteink: $84, or around 15% off the usual $99 price.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

The non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is the best Kindle deal most people should buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. This is a good option if you don't care about maxing out storage or getting rid of lock screen ads.

If you read a lot of material that uses color, like comics or some colored manga, the extra money for a color e-reader is definitely worth it. Check out the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft for a good option.
